rows.author: H069;
rows.title_full: COMMEMORATION OF THE HACIENDA LUISITA MASSACRE
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Hicap initially extended Anakpawis´ sympathy to the victims of super Typhoon Yolanda. In commemoration of the ninth anniversary of the Hacienda Luisita Massacre last November 16, 2013, Rep. Hicap said that up to the present, justice has not yet been given to those who died in the massacre, and that the farmers are still awaiting for the
land that they have been fighting for. He noted that under the present administration, everything that the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) is doing to implement any Supreme Court decision is in the interest of the Cojuangco-Aquino family. While it would seem that the DAR is implementing the Supreme Court decision to distribute lands to the farmer-beneficiaries, Rep. Hicap said that the illegal and immoral control of the Cojuangco-Aquino family of Hacienda Luisita remains. He maintained that the military and police are deployed in the Hacienda and added that no genuine land distribution is happening therein.
He then called for a free distribution of land in
Hacienda Luisita, collective land ownership for
farmers and farmworkers, abolition of the Cojuangco-Aquino family´s monopoly of land, and
genuine land reform and justice for the Hacienda
Luisita peasantry.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Both speaking in Filipino, Reps. Dela Cruz and
Hicap delved into the real situation in Hacienda
Luisita and the problems being encountered as to the distribution of lands therein in light of a final and executory Supreme Court decision on the matter. Rep. Hicap predicted that genuine land reform in Hacienda Luisita will not happen under the PNoy Administration and then asked the Committee on Agrarian Reform to conduct an onsite hearing to determine the status of the implementation of the said Supreme Court decision.
(SOURCE: Journal No.27,p.8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F122;
rows.title_full: SUPREME COURT DECISION ON THE P D A F
rows.title_short: Oversight Function Of Congress On Setting Budgets
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Ortega (F.), the Chair recognized Rep. Dela Cruz from Party-List Abakada who expressed his views on the recent Supreme Court decision declaring the PDAF as unconstitutional. While he lauded the High Tribunal for reiterating the need for Congress to strongly and seriously pursue its constitutional power of the purse, he lamented how it harshly condemned the congressional pork barrel fund without due regard to its many benefits to the people. With the abolition of the PDAF, Rep. Dela Cruz urged Congress to consider ways and means to provide basic services in a timely and responsible manner;
be more vigilant in exercising its powers and
prerogatives including the legislative oversight of the President´s Special Purpose Fund and the Judiciary´s Judicial Development Fund; and closely scrutinize the proposal to provide funds for the relief, rehabilitation and reconstruction of calamity-ravaged areas
and subject it to legal and constitutional budgetary procedures.
(SOURCE: Journal No.27,pp.8&9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F100;
rows.title_full: SUPREME COURT DECISION ON THE P D A F
rows.title_short: P D A F As Unconstitutional
rows.abstract:
Rep. Colmenares focused on the recent Supreme
Court(SC) decision declaring as unconstitutional the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) or other similar lump-sum items, and opined that
eliminating the pork barrel of the Congressmen and Senators would not stop graft and corruption and patronage politics as long as the presidential pork exists. He thereafter referred to the SC opinion of Congress´ invalid delegation of power because of the lump-sum items in the national budget, and pointed out that the President´s use of his lump-sum fund
would mean allowing him to exercise invalid
appropriation powers and also giving him the power to legislate. He likewise emphasized that the President´s approving the General Appropriations Act containing allocations that are not itemized would also mean violating the doctrine of presentment, as Congress has no way of determining whether the President would approve or disapprove a project with wisdom.
Finally, he suggested the use of the calamity fund for the victims of Typhoon Yolanda and other similar natural disasters through an itemized supplemental budget, and asked the High Tribunal to also declare the presidential pork as unconstitutional.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 28,pp.11,15-16)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Barzaga, Biazon, Dela Cruz, Padilla and Tinio. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F093;
rows.title_full: INTERNATIONAL DAY OF THE ELIMINATION OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ilagan initially stressed that the Philippines, for the first time, joins the international community in celebrating the National Consciousness Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, and recalled how the movement against the state-inflicted persecution and death of two Latin American women had evolved into a global effort to end discrimination and violence against women and children. She said that after ten years, Gabriela´s efforts in crafting the measure enjoining government agencies and departments in marking November 25 for said commemoration has resulted in the signing of Republic Act (RA) No. 10398. She lamented that despite efforts to protect women and children, the Philippine National Police (PNP) and some women and children advocacy groups have reported several cases of rape, attempted rape, trafficking, child pornography and cyber prostitution. She attributed these to poverty and lack of basic and social services exacerbated by the
onslaught of natural and man-made disasters, as well as police and military abuse especially in the provinces. She thereafter asked her colleagues to support Gabriela and other concerned sectors and to approve measures to protect women and children against violence and injustice.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr.
discussed with Rep. Ilagan the women in Metro
Manila who were victims of robbery, rape and
murder, and opined that these crimes proliferate
because of the failure by the authorities to efficiently solve them and punish the perpetrators accordingly. Rep. Atienza expressed his concerns on the following: 1) the alarming increase of crimes aside from those which have not been reported as some victims no longer file complaints; 2) the deliberate failure of the police force to immediately respond to victims and apprehend criminals because of their
extracurricular activities; and 3) the generally
deteriorating peace and order situation in the urban areas of the country especially in Metro Manila. Asking for the Members´ commitment, he then urged the House leadership to look into and evaluate the performance of the police ranks.
(SOURCE: Journal No.28,pp.16-17)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G105;
rows.title_full: PLIGHT OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN SURVIVORS OF TYPHOON YOLANDA
rows.abstract:
Rep. De Jesus brought to the attention of her
colleagues the plight of the victims of Typhoon
Yolanda in the Visayas to underscore the encouraging multisectoral relief efforts of Gabriela Women´s Party-List (Lingap Gabriela) and the pressing issues pertaining to the scarce presence, inadequate government relief efforts and dismal conditions of the victims. She cited in particular her personal account of the absence of basic services by government agencies and local government units in Leyte and in Samar that can be gleaned from the lack of shelter, unattended and uncollected corpses, dearth
of relief food supplies, gradual reconstruction of infrastructures, and lack of adequate medical services for victims of trauma and distress.
Whereupon Rep. De Jesus stated that there are
things that Congress should look into with vigilance such as 1) itemized allocation of funds for social services for the calamity victims; and 2) transparency as to where the billions of pesos that the country received as help from other countries would go. She
thereafter called on her colleagues to visit the
provinces that were affected by super Typhoon
Yolanda.(SOURCE: Journal No.29,p.8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H025;
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE REHABILITATION OF THE BONIFACIO MONUMENT IN CALOOCAN CITY
rows.title_short: 150th Birth Anniversary Of Gat Andres Bonifacio
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Bondoc, the Chair recognized
Rep. Edgar R. Erice from the Second District of
Caloocan City who spoke in Filipino to pay tribute to Andres Bonifacio on his 150th birth anniversary on November 30, 2013. He informed the Body that for the first time in the history of its celebration, a President of the nation would visit his monument. He narrated that although Bonifacio was from Tondo, the katipuneros held their meetings in Caloocan and
after the death of his first wife, he married Gregoria de Jesus from Caloocan. He pointed out that like the national hero Gat Jose Rizal, Bonifacio also played a big role in the nation´s democracy and then traced the history of the Bonifacio monument in Caloocan City that was designed by National Artist Guillermo Estrella Tolentino on August 29, 1930. He likewise urged the Members to support and include in the 2015 proposed national budget the funds for the redevelopment and enhancement of the Bonifacio monument and hoped that due care and concern would be provided to redevelop said monument.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. CHIPECO
Rep. Chipeco commended Rep. Erice for his speech and on behalf of his constituents, expressed
solidarity with the celebration of the 150th birth anniversary of Gat Andres Bonifacio. He expressed optimism that the proposal of Rep. Erice for the redevelopment and re-enhancement of the monument of Bonifacio would come into reality and also pave the way for providing sufficient attention to honoring Jose Rizal and other national heroes in monuments located in various areas throughout the country. Rep. Erice concurred therewith.
(SOURCE: Journal No.29,p.8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Chipeco. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G102;
rows.title_full: KEY DECISIONS ADOPTED AT THE WARSAW CLIMATE CHANGE CONFERENCE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Yap delved on the just concluded 19th
Conference of Parties to the United Nations
Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) held in Warsaw, Poland. She said that this year´s conference is of paramount significance to
the Philippines considering that super Typhoon
Yolanda just hit the country. As a member of the
congressional delegation to said conference, Rep.
Yap reported out that the Warsaw negotiations were important so as to determine the pathway for an agreement that the party-countries aim to complete in Paris in December 2015 and which is expected to take effect by 2020. She added that the agreement included commitments to adopt a new and comprehensive program to address the climate crisis. Rep. Yap also pointed out that the Philippines in particular, is optimistic about the program Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation plus pro-forest activities (REDD+) for its potential in
spurring the country´s reforestation efforts. She said that while the Warsaw conference was not able to achieve a breakthrough in the fight against climate change, it put in place some building blocks necessary for a treaty to be forged in 2015 in Paris. Thereafter, Rep. Yap asked for her colleagues´ support for the Sustainable Forest Management Bill which aims to provide strategies and programs for protection and sustainable management of forest ecosystems that will enhance the promotion of ecosystem services, mitigate and adapt to climate change impacts. She also asked for the approval of
the Delineation of Forest Limits Bill which provides the basis for the implementation of protection, conservation and development initiatives within forest land boundaries.
(SOURCE: Journal No.29,pp.8&9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F102;
rows.title_full: REACTION TO SPEECH DELIVERED BY COMMISSIONER NADEREV SANO OF THE CLIMATE CHANGE COMMISSION AT THE WARSAW CLIMATE CHANGE CONFERENCE
rows.title_short: Honoring Comm. Sano And Mr. Tanchuling
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello paid homage to Commission on Climate Change Commissioner Naderev Saño and the late Mr. Milo Tanchuling, former Secretary General of the Freedom from Debt Coalition. He stressed that Commissioner Saño was the country´s
lead negotiator in the recently concluded climate
change talks in Warsaw, Poland and became the face, not only of the Philippines, but also of the developing countries when he appealed to big climate polluters to make radical emission cuts after arguing that Typhoon Yolanda was a product of climate change caused principally by the uncontrolled emissions of greenhouse gases of rich industrialized countries. He stated that Mr. Tanchuling on the other hand, exemplified the finest in public service as he made efforts to reduce the country´s unfair debt obligations
to the big international banks, opposed the Automatic Appropriations Law and fought against the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA). In closing, Rep. Bello stated that Commissioner
Saño and Mr. Tanchuling are both inspiring examples that the Filipino people, especially the youth, could be proud of as they have earned their mark as very important figures who have contributed to a vibrant civil society in the Philippines.
(SOURCE: Journal No.29,pp.9&10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G079;
rows.title_full: INTERIM MINDANAO ELECTRICTY MARKET
rows.title_short: I M E M Electric Price Increase In Mindanao
rows.abstract:
Rep. Rodriguez rose to denounce the government
imposition of a wholesale electricity spot market
called the Interim Mindanao Electricity Market
(IMEM) which he said was in utter disregard of the provisions of the EPIRA Law and in violation of the fundamental economic principles governing the establishment of competitive electricity market. He claimed that the IMEM, among others, will increase immensely the price of electricity in Mindanao by as much as ten times the present rate and will increase the profits of independent power producers (IPPs) who own the oil-fueled plants in Mindanao by as much as 20 times their present profits. He thereafter revealed that the power shortages in Mindanao were artificial and man-made, and not caused by droughts as the government wanted the people to believe; and that the reduction in the capacity of the power plants was due to the incompetence and negligence of the Power Sector Assets and Liabilities Management (PSALM) Corporation-National Power Corporation (NPC) as well as PSALM´s reduction of power supply contracts for the distribution of utilities throughout the region. He then asked the Department of Energy (DOE) to defer the implementation of the IMEM until lawful conditions could justify the establishment of an electricity market in Mindanao. As he stressed that said deferment is also being pursued by the Mindanao Coalition of Power Consumers and other concerned sectors, he asked Congress to support this initiative as well as to investigate the circumstances
that brought about the establishment of the IMEM
and the cause of the deterioration of power plants managed by PSALM throughout Mindanao.
(SOURCE: Journal No.29,pp.10-11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Masongsong and Seneres. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G113;
rows.title_full: MONOPOLY IN THE L P G INDUSTRY
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ty talked about his position on the looming
monopoly in the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)
industry, with the LPG already being considered as a basic necessity in people´s everyday lives especially in the urban areas. He pointed out that the LPG is one of the products covered in the Downstream Oil Industry Deregulation Act of 1998 or Republic Act (RA) No. 8479 which declared as a State policy the liberalization and deregulation of the oil industry to ensure a truly competitive market under a regime of
fair prices and adequate and continuous supply of
environmentally-clean and high-quality products.
While the law sought to promote and encourage
the entry of new participants in the industry, Rep. Ty voiced his concern over the recent public disclosures that the second largest LPG firm in the country, Liquigaz Philippines Corporation, is being put up for sale by its parent firm, SHV Energy of the Netherlands. He maintained that the three big oil companies namely, Petron, Shell and Chevron (Caltex) are the potential buyers of the company which could result to the elimination of other players.
To prevent the big industry players from
monopolizing the business of small and independent LPG refillers and marketers, he urged the House to immediately: 1) conduct an investigation, in aid of legislation, on the looming monopoly in the LPG industry; and 2) amend RA No. 8479 to strengthen its anti-trust safeguards or pass the long overdue Anti-
Trust Law.
(SOURCE: Journal No.30,p.7 & 8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G064;
rows.title_full: IMPORTANCE OF PDAF TO HOUSE MEMBERS
rows.title_short: Eulogy For P D A F
rows.abstract:
Rep. Nograles spoke of the recent announcement
of the Supreme Court declaring the Priority
Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) as
unconstitutional. He cited survey figures showing
that people were less aware of congressional projects but wanted the Senators and House Members to continue delivering them as much as altogether making laws, investigating anomalies, and passing the national budget. He asked how projects could continue without the PDAF which Congress had deleted in the 2014 GAA and which the Supreme Court had ruled against. While he stressed his desire to continue being a representative of the people, he also explained the positive features of a parliamentary form of government.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LOONG
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Tupay T.
Loong asked why the Supreme Court had issued said
decision as he cited the Members´ role, the
sentiments of the PDAF beneficiaries, and the
PDAF´s inclusion in the national budget. Rep.
Nograles clarified that what the Supreme Court did not want wasthe postenactmentidentification of projects; and pointed out that promising projects during election campaigns was part of historical practice since 1922. Considering that the Supreme Court has also prohibited congressional insertions into the budget,
aside from declaring the PDAF as unconstitutional, Reps. Loong and Nograles next delved on the actions that should be undertaken by the House to regain the power of the purse. Both Members agreed that Congress should consider shifting to a parliamentary form of government in order to hold the Executive
Department accountable for the programs and
projects of their constituents.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAQUIZ
To the queries of Rep. Paquiz, Rep. Nograles
stated that considering the abolition of the PDAF, Congress should exercise its oversight functions to ensure that the Executive Department implements projects and programs for their constituents; craft measures that will institutionalize reforms in the government; and investigate government agencies that are not doing their responsibilities. He said that it
is incumbent upon the leadership of Congress to
educate and explain to the people their new role as legislators considering that they have been stripped off of one of their major functions.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. CHIPECO
Reps. Chipeco and Nograles discussed the issue
of changing the present form of government from
presidential to parliamentary system in light of the Supreme Court decision, with the latter expressing his willingness to sponsor a measure calling for such purpose to sustain the reforms of good governance. They thereafter dwelled on the need for Congress to reorganize and fully perform its oversight functions in monitoring the various departments with respect to the needs of their constituents.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 30,p.8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Loong, Paquiz and Chipeco. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H065;
rows.title_full: BIRTHDAY OF THE LATE FORMER SEN. NINOY AQUINO
rows.abstract:
In commemoration of the birth anniversary of the
late Senator Benigno Aquino Jr., Rep. Atienza said that the Members should never forget how the former gave up his life for the freedom, liberty and democracy that the Filipino people now enjoy. He stressed that during the martial law years, Mr. Aquino suffered under detention for the ideals that he never gave up; inspired other people who died in their fight for the country´s freedom; and sacrificed his life for
the sake of democracy. He however stressed that
whatever cause Mr. Aquino started would be for
naught if the people would not value the real
meaning of freedom and human rights. He underscored the need to unite in helping the country recover from the onslaught of natural calamities, and to be inspired by how Mr. Aquino lived his life in facing the many challenges the people are now confronted with.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BANAL
At the outset, Rep. Banal commended Rep.
Atienza for reminding the importance of the birth
anniversary of the late Senator Aquino. Reacting to the latter´s claim that the government has done nothing on this important day, Rep. Banal informed the Body of the holding of an activity to promote the love of reading for children dubbed as “Araw ng Pagbasa, Araw ng Pag-asa” as part of the culminating activity of the Department of Education; declaring the whole month of November as a National Reading
Month; and the organization of storytelling sessions in some public schools all over the country. He then invited Rep. Atienza to join in or share his or his Party-List´s ideas in the pursuit of similar undertakings in the future.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Stating his concern that some Filipinos may have
already forgotten the sacrifices of a great leader, Rep. Dela Cruz congratulated Rep. Atienza for sending a wake up call to the House of Representatives and the Filipino people, especially in these times of misery and disaster. Both Members then discussed the
importance and contributions of the late Senator
Aquino to Philippine democracy and the possible
government activities aimed at commemorating the
lives of the nation´s heroes as well as other important events in Philippine history.
(SOURCE: Journal No.30,p.9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Banal and Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H072;
rows.title_full: U.S. MILITARY PRESENCE IN THE RELIEF OPERATIONS VIS-A-VIS INTERNATIONAL TREATY ON DISASTER RESPONSE
rows.title_short: Rotational Presence Of U S Troops
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ridon strongly denounced the statement
made by Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA)
Secretary Albert Del Rosario on the humanitarian
response and relief efforts of the United States (US) to the Philippines in the aftermath of Typhoon Yolanda as demonstrative of a pressing need to expedite the ongoing negotiations between the two countries that would allow increased rotational presence of US troops in the Philippines. He recalled the underlying motive of the US military deployment to countries stricken by disasters like Haiti and the Philippines and opined that assistance to victims of the disaster can proceed independently of the Visiting Forces Agreement or
the RP-US Mutual Defense Treaty. In light thereof, he called on the DFA and the national government to stand guard against US exploitation of the humanitarian crisis in central Philippines by taking the lead in the signing of an international legal framework for disaster response; and drafting a multilateral disaster response treaty allowing maximum international solidarity and participation in times of disaster without undermining sovereignty. (SOURCE: Journal No.30,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F048;
rows.title_full: GARNISHMENT OF REP. PACQUIAO'S ASSETS
rows.title_short: Tax Raps Against Rep. Manny Pacquiao
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Belmonte (J.), the Chair recognized Rep. Emil L. Ong from the Second District of Northern Samar who questioned the timing of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) regarding Rep. Emmanuel D. Pacquiao´s nonpayment of taxes considering that the latter has not only given the country much honor with his unprecedented record of eight prestigious international boxing titles but is also a
respected Member of the House of Representatives.
He then urged the Body to pass a resolution condemning the ill-timing action by the BIR Commissioner. INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Reps. Dela Cruz and Ong discussed the
questionable motive by the BIR´s advisory on Rep.
Pacquiao´s deficient tax payments; and the former´s suggestion for the latter to include BIR assessment and collection processes, especially for big taxpayers in his resolution regarding the Bureau´s action in the
case of Rep. Pacquiao.
REFERRAL OF REP. ONG´S
PRIVILEGE SPEECH
On motion of Rep. Belmonte (J.), there being no
objection, the Body referred the privilege speech of
Rep. Ong and the interpellation thereon to the
appropriate Committee.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: A007;
rows.title_full: EXPRESSED GRATITUDE TO INDIVIDUALS AND OGANIZATIONS WHO PROVIDED AID TO THE VICTIMS OF TYPHOON YOLANDA
rows.title_short: Gratitude To Those Who Helped Typhoon Yolanda's Victims
rows.abstract:
Rep. Apostol rose to appeal to the government
agencies concerned to expedite the repair of damaged infrastructure in the Second District of Leyte, and to express his utmost gratitude, in behalf of his constituents, for the outpouring of assistance that they received in the aftermath of super Typhoon Yolanda from the President and other Executive agencies,
Members of Congress, private companies and nongovernment organizations, whose names he read into the records.
(SOURCE: Journal No.31,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2014-01-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F100;
rows.title_full: DELAYED IMPLEMENTATION OF RA 10368 - GRANTING COMPENSATION TO VICTIMS OF HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS DURING THE MARCOS REGIME
rows.title_short: Unimplemented Human Rigts Victim's Reparation And Recognition Act
rows.abstract:
Rep. Colmenares delved on the Marcos Human Rights Compensation Act which Congress passed a
year ago. He however lamented to date the refusal of President Benigno S. Aquino III to implement said law and appoint the members of the Compensation Board that would give recognition and reparation to the human rights victims during martial law. He stressed that he cannot fathom the reason of the President for not implementing the law considering that the compensation money came from a Swiss bank and not from the government coffers. Stating that he himself was a human rights victim during
martial law, he said that he cannot benefit from the compensation package considering that he is one of the main authors of the law. He stressed that the refusal of the President to implement the Human Rights Compensation Act would delay the application process of the thousands of victims who have long waited for recognition from the government for the violation of their human rights, some of whom are now old or have already died. He then urged his colleagues to use their oversight functions and investigate the reasons of the President for his continuing refusal to implement the law and likewise enjoined the human rights victims to assert their rights under the law.
(SOURCE: Journal No.31,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2014-01-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H068;
rows.title_full: NEED TO IMMEDIATELY ADDRESS THE RISING INCIDENCE OF HIV-AIDS IN THE COUNTRY
rows.title_short: H I V / A I D S
rows.abstract:
Rep. Gutierrez rose to commemorate the observance
of World AIDS Day and discuss the urgent issues related to HIV/AIDS. As he noted the beginning of the country´s declaration of war against the
disease with the passage of Republic Act (RA) No.
8504 or the Philippine AIDS Prevention and Control Act of 1998, he cited the government´s action in curbing and stabilizing the spread of HIV and AIDS and the positive developments in the global arena. Considering the rise in the number of HIV/AIDS cases in the last 15 years and the shifting trends as well as changing dynamics in the demographics of people affected by the disease, Rep. Gutierrez stressed the need for Congress to craft measures that will prevent and control its spread. He said that despite
government efforts to address this concern, the
treatment and prevention is largely saddled by the country´s traditional values and culture thus giving the people a limited understanding of the disease. He then cited cases of continuing stigma and discrimination against the victims and their families; emphasized the need to equip the people with information on how to stay healthy and avoid HIV/AIDS infection;
and stressed the need to provide adequate funds
to the health sector to enable it to perform its tasks of giving treatment and support services to the affected persons.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 31,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2014-01-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F057;
rows.title_full: COMMEMORATION OF MINDANAO PEACE WEEK
rows.abstract:
Rep. Rodriguez stated that the day marks the culmination of the Mindanao Week of Peace, a weeklong commemoration of the desire for genuine and lasting peace in Mindanao. He lamented that the country has grown weary of the continuous insurgency problems in the area, and that attempts to resolve the social and economic concerns of its people have taken a backseat because of other issues and calamities now besetting the nation. As a trueborn Mindanaoan, he enjoined his colleagues to be more
compassionate to their brothers and sisters, especially the silent majority who has become casualties of war. He thereafter referred to the signing in 2012 of the Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro (FAB) which represents the dreams of the entire Bangsamoro people, and which further ignited when early in the year, the President issued Executive Order (EO) No. 120 creating the Transition Commission on the Bangsamoro that will draft the Bangsamoro
Basic Law and ensure that its charter will
reflect the goals and aspirations of its people.
After describing the status of the annexes to the
FAB which are still being formulated, Rep. Rodriguez urged his colleagues to give the proper democratic processes a chance to work. He also called on the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) and the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) to unite for the peace and development of their region. Thereafter, on motion of Rep. Sherwin N. Tugna, the Chair recognized Rep. Roy V. Señeres Sr. for his interpellation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Rep. Señeres discussed with Rep. Rodriguez (R.)
the apparent lack of involvement of the MNLF and
Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters (BIFF) in
the government´s current peace talks with the MILF, as well as the importance of the participation of all rebel groups for a successful peace negotiation in Mindanao.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Thereupon, Rep. Rodriguez (R.) took note of and
commended Rep. Seneres´ contributions to the peace process in Mindanao, especially in the forging of the government´s peace accord with the MNLF during the Ramos Administration. He also agreed that all stakeholders to the Bangsamoro issue should be consulted to bring about lasting and inclusive peace in the region.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 31,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2014-01-20
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Seneres. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G105;
rows.title_full: WTO's IMPACT ON WOMEN ISSUES
rows.abstract:
Rep. De Jesus conveyed the advocacies and visions
collectively shared by the different countries
and communities around the world during the recent People´s Global Camp held in Bali, Indonesia where she represented the country´s women sector. Citing pertinent articles in the Declaration of the said People´s Global Camp, Rep. De Jesus underscored the importance of upholding the principles on international relations based on human rights, solidarity,
equality and cooperation and highlighted the
7 universal call of the Camp and its participants for a just framework for trade and development gearing towards the realization of the people´s economic, political, social and cultural being.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.35,pp.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H069;
rows.title_full: PRICE HIKES OF PETROLEUM PRODUCTS
rows.title_short: Price Hikes On Oil And Electricity
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Hicap stood to share
the sentiments and opposition of the Filipino people to the alarming and continuous increase in the prices of electricity, oil and other petroleum products, and some basic goods and services. Specifically, he pointed out that the additional increase in electricity rates would greatly affect the minimum wage earners as well as the middle class earners who have already felt the brunt of the increase in the prices of public utilities and services. Considering that the country has not yet recovered from the damages brought about by super typhoon Yolanda, he held accountable the national government for allowing said increase in favor of oil cartels and electric companies; and Congress for the
enactment of the Downstream Oil Industry
Deregulation Law and the Electric Power Industry
Reform Act (EPIRA). He said that since the 13th
Congress, Anakpawis Party-List has continuously
filed measures seeking the repeal of said laws and then urged the Members to support them.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.35,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F102;
rows.title_full: GATT-WTO AGREEMENTS IMPACT ON PHILIPPINE AGRICULTURE
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Ortega (F.), the Chair
recognized Rep. Walden F. Bello of Party-List
Akbayan who spoke about the recently concluded
World Trade Organization (WTO) Ministerial
meeting in Bali, Indonesia. He argued on the
implications of the provisions pertaining to trade facilitation initiatives and the restrictions on agriculture subsidy program by developing countries in the WTO meeting.
He cited in particular the initial disagreement of developing countries to the WTO proposals,
particularly on the so-called extension of the
agriculture subsidy program to only four years to
underscore that the Bali package is unbalanced and disadvantageous in view of the absence of any
commitment and refusal of developed countries to
reduce their agricultural subsidies which result in the dumping of agricultural products in less developed countries. He also took exception to the concurrence of Trade and Industry Secretary Gregory Domingo with the WTO provisions on trade facilitation and revision of the four-year agricultural subsidy extension limit. He maintained that Secretary Domingo has not fully
realized the lessons of past disadvantageous trade agreements under the WTO to negotiate a
commitment from the developed countries of
reducing agricultural subsidies and moreover, to
determine exactly the absence of a clear economic
advantage for the Philippines out of the Bali package. These are the issues that he would like to ask of Secretary Domingo, he stated.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.35,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GLOBALIZATION AND WTO since 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: B006;
rows.title_full: REACTION TO ALLEGED NON-FILING OF THE STATEMENT OF ELELCTION CONTRIBUTORS AND EXPENDITURES (SOCE) TO THE COMELEC BY CERTAIN ELECTED OFFICIALS
rows.title_short: Non Filing Of S O C E
rows.abstract:
Rep. Balindong stood to defend his integrity and
honor as well as that of other elected government
officials on their alleged nonfiling of their Statement of Contributions and Expenditures (SOCE) as announced by the Commission on Elections (Comelec) through newspaper reports and television news the previous week. He then related to his colleagues how the Comelec
officials corrected their mistake of including him in the list of subject officials after he showed them a copy of the SOCE which he knew he had filed. According to the Comelec, he added, the database of its regional office in the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) was not updated; hence, there was no file of his SOCE on record. While he bears no grudge to the Comelec officials, he advised them to be more circumspect and careful the next time they believe that they have uncovered an election
anomaly. Thereafter, Rep. Balindong expressed hope that in the pursuit of their respective duties, they could contribute to good governance without resorting to careless accusations which can cause damage not only to government officials but to government institutions
as well. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,p.13)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F087;
rows.title_full: AFTERMATH OF TYPHOON YOLANDA IN THE 4TH DISTRICT OF CEBU
rows.abstract:
Rep. Salimbangon initially asked for continuous
help for areas hit by supertyphoon Yolanda and
pointed out that like Tacloban City, his own district in Cebu experienced unimaginable death, injury, and destruction. Citing a recent earthquake that also wreaked devastation in Bohol, he said that the nation´s officials should admit their shortcomings during calamities and set aside their differences in order to help their distressed countrymen.
Subsequently, Rep. Salimbangon cited his coordinative relief efforts with various government agencies in the aftermath of the typhoon. However, he rued some instances of politicking in the distribution and delivery of Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) relief packs. Even as he said that the DSWD allowed him to use the balance of his 2012 Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) to purchase relief packs, he also expressed
the dilemma of helping in future calamities but not having PDAF anymore. As he cited government reports on destruction to infrastructure, crops, livestock, and communication and transportation, he also urged the Body to bail out the electric cooperatives who had secured loans to restore power. On behalf of his constituents and all those affected by typhoon Yolanda, Rep. Salimbangon expressed his gratitude to the different entities, charitable organizations and foundations, business sectors and to his colleagues in the Visayan bloc for their
valued kindness and boundless generosity in helping his constituents to recover and rebuild their lives. He also thanked His Excellency U Thein Sein of the Republic of Myanmar for his visit to Bantayan Island and all the Members of Congress for the immediate approval of the P14.6 billion supplemental rehabilitation fund. Even as he welcomed the appointment of former Senator Panfilo Lacson as the new rehabilitation czar, Rep. Salimbangon expressed hope that the intended
rehabilitation budget would be shared equally
among the affected areas. Considering the abolition of the PDAF, he appealed to his colleagues to consider the inclusion of P10 billion as a calamity fund in the budget of Congress for the year 2014 to be administered by the Office of the Speaker subject to all government regulations as he stated that each
Member of Congress must be given the chance to get involved in the rebuilding of his/her own district.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,pp.13-15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Suarez and Dela Cruz. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules

rows.author: F068;
rows.title_full: STRENGTHENING RP-HONGKONG RELATIONSHIP
rows.abstract:
Rep. Singson adverted to the continuing strain in
foreign relations between the Philippine national
government and the local government of Hong Kong
on the issue of the August 23, 2010 hostage-taking incident in Luneta Park which resulted in the death of Chinese nationals and the alleged incompetence of Philippine law enforcement authorities in handling the hostage crisis. He underscored the implications of the incident to the employment of and travel sanctions
against overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in
Hong Kong. He maintained that while the local government of Hong Kong requests for a formal apology from the Philippine national government regarding the said incident, the latter has remained indifferent to the request. He stressed that on behalf of the Filipino people, he would like to express a formal apology to the seven million-strong citizens of Hong Kong and
enjoined the Members to coauthor a resolution which he hoped will finally resolve the misunderstanding between the citizens of Hong Kong and the Philippine government. He thereafter requested the Members to rise and
observe a moment of prayer as a sign of respect to the casualties of the Luneta hostage-taking incident. 
(SOURCE: Journal No.36,pp.23-24)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Atienza and Erice. Manifestation by Rep.Seneres. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H068;
rows.title_full: COMMEMORATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS DAY
rows.abstract:
Rep. Gutierrez spoke about the issue of human
rights, dignity and freedom in commemoration of the December 10 celebration of International Human Rights Day, which he said, also fell on the 65th anniversary of the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR). He pointed out that the Philippines was one of the 48 countries that signed the 1948 Declaration and since then, it is one of the world´s leading countries in the formal and legal recognition
and articulation of human rights principles.
Unfortunately however, he said that the Philippines´ experience with human rights is not a tale of articulation and achievement. He averred that in the 26 years since People Power allowed the adoption of a “human rights Constitution,” human rights violations continued despite the sincere and valiant efforts of government institutions and nongovernment human
rights communities. Thus, he maintained that
there is now the challenge to recapture the commitment to uphold human rights by redefining the agenda, approach and strategy in dealing with the human rights issues of the times.
Rep. Gutierrez stressed that the bleak and discouraging state of human rights continued during President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo´s tenure and persists in the P-Noy administration. He cited the Maguindanao Massacre and the dragging prosecution of the perpetrators thereof in the former; and the inaction on the National Human Rights Action Plan and continuing human rights violations in the latter. He thus urged the Executive and Congress to prioritize
human rights, evaluate triumphs and setbacks,
acknowledge mistakes, and punish the wrongdoers.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,p.24)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. Rules.

rows.author: H072;
rows.title_full: COMMEMORATION OF THE LIFE AND WORKS OF NELSON MANDELA
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ridon paid tribute to former South African
President Nelson Mandela who died on December 5,
2013. He related the leader´s anti-apartheid advocacy starting from his university years and founding of the African National Congress Youth League and Umkhontro we Sizwe (Spear of the Nation) up to his incarceration for two times. He stressed that the 1993 Nobel Peace Prize winner and symbol of moral and competent leadership worked for racial reconciliation,
nationalization and freedom against foreign
domination, the rights of marginalized sectors of society, and the upliftment of the general welfare of his countrymen. He then asked his fellow Filipinos to remember and apply Mandela´s legacy to the local political and socioeconomic situation.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,p.24)
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H080;
rows.title_full: ON THE SECURITY OF TENURE OF BUREAU OF CUSTOMS EMPLOYEES
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Señeres
from the OFW Party-List said that the Office of the President (OP), Department of Finance (DOF), and Bureau of Customs (BOC) were trampling on the
following provisions of the Constitution under the guise of reorganizing or reforming the BOC: workers´ security of and protection of rights, right to human dignity, and right to due process. He discussed their plan to decapitate the bureau´s top 50 officials which had also raised fear of removal/replacement among the rank-and-file. After citing several Supreme Court decisions on government reorganization and security of tenure, Rep. Señeres asked the relevant House committees to conduct an inquiry on the issue and the agencies concerned to suspend their action thereon.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,p.25)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G113;
rows.title_full: ON THE CAUSES OF LPG PRICE HIKES
rows.title_short: Shortage Of L P G ( Liquefied Petroleum Gas)
rows.abstract:
The Chair then recognized Rep. Ty who asked
the Body to investigate the scheduled price increase of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) whose international contract price had already gone up, saying it was immoral, reprehensible, and unscrupulous. He pointed out that the public was already suffering higher costs of electricity, fuel, and basic commodities especially during the current holiday season. He observed that Shell Philippines´ untimely shutdown of storage facilities under the guise of maintenance,
which resulted in an LPG shortage, seemed to follow a pattern. He raised the possibility of collusion among the industry´s big players and cited the request of the Department of Energy for Congress to amend the Electric Power Industry Reform Act(EPIRA).
(SOURCE: House Journal No.36,p.25)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H057;
rows.title_full: STRENGTHENING HIV-AIDS POLICIES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tambunting focused on the rapid increase in
the incidence of HIV-AIDS in the Philippines as
evidenced by the data and statistics that he
mentioned. During the 19th ASEAN Summit in Bali,
Indonesia, Rep. Tambunting said, the Philippines was one of the countries that had reaffirmed its
commitment to achieving the global target of getting to zero new HIV infections, zero discrimination, and zero AIDS-related deaths. However, he said that while the rest of the world has either halted the spread or reduced the number of new infections, the Philippines´ trajectory seemed to be towards the opposite direction, even as the country was able to
legislate a law that was once hailed as a model
legislation in Asia and the Pacific. He then called on his colleagues to unite towards
attaining zero new HIV infections, zero
discrimination and zero AIDS-related deaths towards an AIDS-free generation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Reps. Señeres and Tambunting discussed the
percentage of HIV-AIDS carriers coming from the
overseas Filipino workers´ (OFW) sector and female sex workers, among others. The former then
reiterated his request that the latter´s speech should be acted upon immediately.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Recognized by the Chair, upon Rep. Binay´s
motion, Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr. commended Rep.
Tambunting for a very concise and precise
description of the problem on the growing number of AIDS cases in the country without resorting to
hysterics and misdirection, and for not saying that the solution to the AIDS problem is contraception and the use of condoms but rather discipline, information and education.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAQUIZ
Rep. Paquiz likewise commended Rep.Tambunting for proposing the adoption of measures to reduce the incidence of HIV-AIDS cases in the country. When asked by the former whether nurses and health workers are needed to promote AIDS
information and education, the latter replied in the affirmative.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAQUIZ
(Continuation)
Rep. Tambunting agreed with Rep. Paquiz that
health workers should be given the right salary and remuneration to enable them to effectively conduct healthful education and thus lower the incidence of HIV-AIDS in the country.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.33,p.16-17)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2014-01-20
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Seneres and Pacquiz. Manifestation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F122;0000;
rows.title_full: MISSING FAKE AND UNREGISTERED SAROs
rows.title_short: Fake S A R O S
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Through his recently filed House Resolution No.
564, Rep. Dela Cruz said he wanted an inquiry into the case of fake and unregistered Special Allotment Release Orders (SAROs). This would enlighten all about the government´s budgetary funding and disbursement systems and practices which have resulted in the loss of millions of pesos for the country and legal ensnarement of some of the Members, he explained. It would also provide an opportunity for those involved to clear their names, he added.
(Continuation)
Winding up his speech, Rep. Dela Cruz explained that he wanted to ensure more information
on and deeper inquiry into the matter.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
On motion of Rep. Lagdameo (M.), the Chair
recognized Rep. Atienza who asked on the topic of
his colleague´s speech.
Contination)
Recognized anew upon Rep. Lagdameo´s (M.)
motion, Rep. Dela Cruz stated that he understood and submitted to the ruling of the Chair. He then read into the records a portion of a report of the Commission on Audit (COA) regarding the questionable SAROs.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.33,p.17)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2014-01-20
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H072;
rows.title_full: W T O MINISTERIAL MEETING IN BALI, INDONESIA
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ridon discussed the first multilateral trade
agreement passed by the World Trade Organization
(WTO) since its creation, in the recent Ninth WTO
Ministerial Conference in Bali, Indonesia. He
stressed that although it was touted as a deal that would result in export, gross output, and employment gains in the global economy, it was also one that introduced unfair trade agreements that would push the economies of developing countries into further bankruptcy and destitution. As he stressed that the Bali package has been presented as a way to ease past mistakes by introducing concessions on food security exemptions and renewed commitments for duty-free trade in order for developing countries and least developed countries (LDCs) to pass the deal on trade facilitation, he however noted that it does not contain any binding agreement for technical and financial
support for developing countries to comply with the new standards. As such, he stated that the Bali package would essentially compel Congress to revise the nation´s laws on taxation, customs and other national economic policies just to accommodate the new WTO policies. Rep. Ridon thereafter enjoined his colleagues to dissent and fight the Bali package because the country does not need concessions and has to overthrow and dissolve the system that continually
perpetrates unfair trade policies.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.33,p.18)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GLOBALIZATION AND WTO since 2014-01-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F093;
rows.abstract:
In the observance of the International Day
against Human Trafficking, Rep. Ilagan rose to
strongly urge Congress to use its policy-making
functions to reverse the government´s labor export program to decisively defeat human trafficking. She stated that fighting human trafficking and exporting human resources are two discordant programs as the government cannot fight human trafficking while actively promoting a program that serves as a vehicle for organized human traffickers. As such, she said that the government has deregulated the environment
for recruitment agencies and labor deployment
abroad, thus making it easy for unscrupulous
individuals to organize and operate illegal
recruitment agencies as in the case of Great Provider Services Exporter (GP) which she mentioned in detail in her speech. Rep. Ilagan thereafter disclosed that the victims and their families are calling on the House to investigate GP´s operation and for the government to stop illegal recruitment and human trafficking. She
also enjoined her colleagues to revisit and abolish, if necessary, the country´s labor export program.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Rep. Señeres manifested his support to the
speech of Rep. Ilagan, and expressed his desire for the authorities to investigate the alleged abuses and acts of human trafficking of the GP firm headed by a certain Mr. Isidro Rodriguez.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 33,p.18)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WELFARE OF CHILDREN since 2014-01-20
rows.remarks: Manifestation of Rep. Seneres. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H081;
rows.title_full: CONTINUING HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Abaya, Rep. Carlos Isagani T. Zarate from Bayan Muna Party-List spoke about the violations of human
rights, as he noted the continuing state of impunity that haunts the people, especially those in the rural areas, and the failure of the counterinsurgency program under the PNoy Administration. He lamented that despite the huge appropriation for Oplan Bayanihan, cases of extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances and bombings continued to rise, and cited cases of military abuse, paramilitary killings and encounters with communist rebels. He urged the government to respond to the call of a human rights group to address the precarious state of
media freedom in the country, and to consider the
plight of political prisoners languishing in various jails throughout the country. As he stressed the President´s failure to form and
convene the Claims Board that is mandated to craft the implementing rules and regulations for the indemnification of the Martial Law victims pursuant to the Human Rights Victims Reparations and Recognition Act, he challenged the President to hasten the prosecution of those involved in the continuing violation of human rights, and asked the Filipino people to continue to fight for their human rights.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.33,p.19)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2014-01-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F103;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Guanlao delved on the issue of rice smuggling in the country which he noted threatens the existence and livelihood of rice farmers as well as the food sufficiency program of the government. He lamented that government efforts against rice smuggling have continued to fail because government officials and enforcement agencies are allegedly in cahoots
with smuggling syndicates. In particular, he
mentioned the accusation made by Bureau of Customs (BOC) Commissioner John Philip Sevilla that certain regional trial court (RTC) judges from Batangas, Davao and Manila have been tolerating or coddling violators of the Tariff and Customs Code as rice smuggling happens in every major port in the country. Rep. Guanlao subsequently urged: 1) the proper government agencies to review and rationalize the rice accreditation process as well as the rules and
regulations of rice traders and others involved in rice trading; 2) the House to support his antismuggling measure House Bill No. 3536; 3) the government to conduct a no-nonsense investigation on the complicity of government officials, judges and enforcement agencies with smuggling syndicates; 4) the BOC to execute legal actions to prevent RTCs from impinging
on customs law; and 5) the Congress to review
laws and policies to strengthen the government´s antismuggling efforts and initiatives. (SOURCE: House Journal No.37pp.1-2)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps.Teves, Padilla, Bondoc and Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G012;
rows.title_full: COMMENDED THE PROVINCE OF PANGASINAN FOR ITS HUMANITARIAN MISSION TO THE VICTIMS OF TYPHOON YOLANDA
rows.title_short: Pangasinan's Help To Victims Of Typhoon \" Yolanda \"
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Bataoil recalled the repeated onslaught of natural and manmade calamities in the country, which he said highlighted the Filipino people´s resilience and ability to recover from disasters and calamities and the innate spirit of bayanihan or volunteerism by all sectors of the society. He claimed that the recent devastation caused by Typhoon Yolanda had not only enabled Filipinos to help those affected by the supertyphoon
but had also provided local government units
(LGUs) the opportunity to show their disaster response readiness and capabilities and humanitarian- relief efforts. Rep. Bataoil informed the Body that the spirit of volunteerism is very much apparent in the humanitarian-relief efforts undertaken by the Provincial Government of Pangasinan in Dulag, Leyte where more than 100 volunteers engaged in medical missions, reconstructed school buildings, provided food and medicines and helped 11 chosen affected families resettle in Pangasinan. He thereafter proceeded with an audio-video presentation of said humanitarian
relief operations. After the presentation, Rep. Bataoil stated that Pangasinan´s assistance to the Yolanda victims in Leyte is a long-term one and added that similar efforts must continue until the calamity victims have fully recovered from the onslaught of the supertyphoon, as well as from the earthquake in Bohol and Cebu, and the MNLF attacks in Zamboanga City. He thereafter asked Filipinos of all faith to join
President Aquino and the whole nation in prayer, to thank the Lord for all the blessings He has bestowed upon everyone.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 37,p.3)
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F093;
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE PASSAGE OF AMENDMENTS TO THE EPIRA
rows.title_short: Electric Power Industry Reform Act ( E P I R A )
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ilagan focused on her concerns regarding
the passage of the Electric Power Industry Reform
Act (EPIRA) which promised lower electricity rates for Filipino households and the industry, as well as the restructuring of the power sector that would have ushered in increased private sector participation in the generation, transmission and distribution of electricity
that will pay off the debts incurred by the National Power Corporation (NPC). However, she said that 13 years after, the promised results under the EPIRA regime remains just a promise. She averred that EPIRA has driven the government into virtual inutility in the face of power rate hikes and added that the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) has been stripped of its powers thus failing to protect energy consumers from the profit-seeking big power industry players.
Rep. Ilagan then asked the Body to rectify the
failure of the EPIRA, thus heeding public calls for relief amidst disaster, calamity and poverty, and to envision an energy sector owned and controlled by the government.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.37,p.3)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F059;
rows.title_full: EXPRESSED GRATITUDE FOR THE CONDOLENCES RECEIVED BY HER FAMILY ON THE DEMISE OF HER HUSBAND, FORMER CONGRESSMAN ANTONINO ROMAN
rows.title_short: Death Of Her Husband, Rep Antonino Roman
rows.abstract:
Rep. Roman rose to extend her gratitude for the
condolences expressed on the demise of his husband, former Rep. Antonino P. Roman. She shared that through the outpouring of love and sympathies and the realization that many lives had been touched by her husband, her family felt honored and blessed to make his passing a constant reminder for them to live
a life of forgiveness, sharing, exploring and love just as what he did while on earth.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,p.1)
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: C072;
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR PEACE, SECURITY AND REHABILITATION IN ZAMBOANGA CITY
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Celso L. Lobregat
initially recalled a privilege speech he delivered in July 2013 wherein he 1) cited the highlights of the Government of the Republic of the Philippines-Moro Islamic Liberation Front (GRP-MILF) peace process from July 2001 to July 2013; 2) pleaded Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) Chairperson Nur Misuari to conduct his group´s activities and pronouncements in the areas of the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM), and not in Zamboanga City; and 3) recommended the inclusion and conformity in the peace agreement of all the stakeholders of Mindanao including Mr. Misuari´s MNLF. He also recounted that in September 2013, the Zamboanga crisis took place which caused havoc and
destruction to lives and properties in his city. Even as the city is now in its rehabilitation phase, he warned, however, that it has been disturbed and threatened anew by an undated letter from the MILF concerning the putting up of the Bangsamoro Political Affairs Office in Barangay Cawit, Zamboanga City which Col. Hashim Zol of the International Monitoring Team (IMT) declared to be illegal and should not be done prior to the signing of the final peace agreement. He emphasized that the people of Zamboanga City had already spoken not to
be part of the ARMM through an overwhelming
referendum vote in 1989 and 2001. While he expressed his support for the peace process, Rep. Lobregat manifested his following requests: for Zamboanga City not to be included in the ARMM or the proposed Bangsamoro; for the Office of the Presidential Adviser on the Peace Process (OPAPP) and the GRP peace panel to conduct genuine consultations prior to the signing of
the peace agreement to be held in Kuala Lumpur that week; and for his speech to be referred immediately to the Committee on Local Government, the Special Committee on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity, and the Committee on National Defense and Security, and for said Committees to immediately conduct committee hearings on the matter.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,p.1)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps.Balindong, Seneres, Sacdalan, Mangudadatu, Tambunting, Dela Cruz and Loong. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F102;
rows.title_full: MOSQUITO INFESTATION IN TYPHOON YOLANDA-AFFECTED AREAS
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello raised his concern on the health issue
of the hapless Yolanda survivors as heavy rains
brought in by Typhoons Yolanda and Agaton had left thousands of small pockets of stagnant water coupled by mountains of debris which converted Tacloban City into a large breeding ground for mosquitoes. He said that the flimsy temporary shelters do not shield the survivors from the hordes of mosquitoes which, if not eradicated, would cause health issues in epidemic
proportions. He then strongly urged the Department of Health (DOH) to immediately take action and conduct necessary measures to kill these mosquitoes and prevent them from breeding. He also urged the government to heed and release the request for P40,000-financial assistance per family in order to fast track their home repair efforts. Stating that majority of the typhoon victims would still have to look for livelihood sources to sustain their needs, Rep. Bello urged everyone to continue sending help, such as foods, medicines and other basic commodities, and encouraged his colleagues to each donate 100 mosquito nets as part of the so-called “mosquito net drive” for the Yolanda victims.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,p.9-10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H069;
rows.title_full: 27th ANNIVERSARY OF THE \"MENDIOLA MASSACRE\"
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Hicap expressed his
sentiments on 1) the continuing struggle of
farmworkers for genuine land reform and social
justice; 2) the unending tension, militarization,
killings and illegal arrests of farmers in Hacienda Luisita Inc. (HLI); 3) the HLI´s failure to totally implement the Stock Distribution Option (SDO) scheme and the Supreme Court decision for free distribution of land to the Hacienda farmworkers; and 4) the alleged conspiracy among the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR), the HLI and the Tarlac Development Corporation (TADECO) regarding the supposed landgrabbing of the Cojuangcos. He also lamented that the present Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program with Extension Reform (CARPER) Law would unlikely be extended beyond 2016 because of the transition plan of the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) to abolish DAR and its recommendation to include lands of public domain as well as alienable, disposable and inalienable lands in land survey and titling.
In closing, Rep. Hicap called on the public and
the whole nation to take part in his party´s advocacy for genuine land reform and social justice.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.38,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G113;
rows.title_full: ON THE ADVERSE EFFECT OF THE SHELL TABANGAO LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASOLINE (LPG) STORAGE DECOMMISSIONING
rows.title_short: Disruption In Liquefied Petroleum Gas (lpg) Supply
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ty delivered a short discourse on the dire
implications in the supply chain of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) as a result of the decommissioning by the Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corporation of Shell Tabangao LPG Storage Terminal in Batangas. Foremost, he mentioned the possible increase in the price of LPGs due to operational costs and the disruption in supply and delivery of LPGs in Southern Luzon and Metro Manila. As part of its advocacy for more affordable and safe LPGs, Rep. Ty thereupon delved on the recommended actions of his Party-List LPGMA to prevent the looming crisis in the cost, delivery, and supply of liquefied petroleum gas. He added that it is imperative
for all stakeholders to ensure that the LPG supply is not disrupted. He thereafter manifested his desire for the House to conduct a congressional inquiry, in aid of legislation, into the impending decommissioning of Shell´s Tabangao LPG Storage Terminal, with the end in view of assuring the continuous supply of and sustainability of LPG products.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.39,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H072;
rows.title_full: FOREIGN ENCROACHMENT INTO LOCAL CABLE TV COMPANIES
rows.title_short: Foreign - Owned Ads On C A T V
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ridon took the floor to raise the issue of the probable encroachment of foreign-owned
corporations in the local cable television (CATV)
industry. He averred that several corporations such as AXN Networks Philippines, Inc. and Fox
International Channels Philippines Corporation are 99.99% foreign-owned and are allegedly engaged in providing programming content, mass media and advertising through the CATV system nationwide which is a clear violation of the 1987 Constitution and several other statutes such as the Foreign Investments Act. He expressed fear that the direct but unwarranted competition of said foreign-owned corporations with legally existing domestic corporations engaged in similar activities pose threats
to the continuing viability of constitutionally
protected domestic industries and employment of
their thousands of workers. He then urged Congress to investigate the state of compliance of the CATV industry, including its operators and programming content providers, with the Philippine Constitution and existing laws, stressing that foreign ownership in the local CATV industry must be stopped and foreign-owned corporations must be held accountable and responsible for their encroachment in the local industry.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.40,p.8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H080;
rows.title_full: ALLEGED EXCESSIVE COLLECTION OF FEES AND/OR PREMIUMS BY PHILHEALTH AND POEA FROM OFWs
rows.title_short: Fat Philhealth And P O E A ( Philippine Overseas Employment Administration ) Allowances And Bonuses
rows.abstract:
The Chair subsequently recognized Rep. Señeres
of OFW Party-List who informed the Members about
several issues pertaining to the alleged impropriety, immorality, and unconstitutionality of the allowances and benefits which the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth) had granted to its officials and employees in 2012 and 2013. He underscored that such grant of bonuses and benefits is not justified, inasmuch as the bulk of PhilHealth´s revenues comes from the forcible exaction and payments of overseas
Filipino workers (OFWs) to the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) of about P2.5 billion yearly or a total of P2,400 for each individual OFW for an annual PhilHealth premium; otherwise, the POEA will not issue the OFW an Overseas Employment Certificate (OEC) to work abroad. He argued that the enforced payments by the OFWs are a curtailment to their right to travel; another form of grave abuse of authority by PhilHealth; and a form of taxation without representation. With all the grievances and complaints of the hundreds of thousands of OFWs falling on deaf ears of the PhilHealth and POEA officials, Rep. Señeres recommended that: 1) the Members concur and support the findings of the Commission on Audit (COA) against PhilHealth for grave abuse of discretion
which is tantamount to large-scale extortion and larceny; 2) the PhilHealth management be summoned to the House to enable the Members to craft laws to protect the citizenry especially the OFWs and refer the matter of grave abuse of discretion in the disbursement of money held in trust by the PhilHealth to appropriate agencies for further investigation and prosecution; 3) the POEA management be likewise summoned for apparently conspiring with PhilHealth for violating the constitutional right of Filipinos to travel; and 4) the House move for the abolition of the OEC requirement of the POEA which the OFWs have complained about as being oppressive, arbitrary and unnecessary. (SOURCE: House Journal No.41,p.4)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H013;
rows.title_full: COMMEMORATING THE 20TH DEATH ANNIVERSARY OF BETTY GO-BELMONTE, THE LATE WIFE OF SPEAKER FELICIANO BELMONTE, JR.
rows.title_short: 20th Death Anniversary Of Betty Go Belmonte
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aragones rose to commemorate the 20th
death anniversary of Mrs. Betty Go-Belmonte, the
late wife of Speaker Belmonte. She stated that Mrs. Go-Belmonte will remain a living memory of an exceptionally talented, kindhearted and God-fearing woman who was so much ahead of her time. She then enjoined her colleagues to remember the life of Mrs. Go-Belmonte as she was an inspiration not only to women but to journalists as well considering that she founded the Philippine Star and the Philippine Daily Inquirer.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.41,p.8)
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H032;
rows.title_full: DEVELOPING THE POTENTIAL OF CLARK AIRPORT AND FREEPORT ZONE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Guiao, through an audio-visual presentation,
discussed the issues that have delayed the development of the Clark International Airport and the Clark Free Port Zone. He stressed that a clear, straightforward and insistent call for the government to prioritize Clark in its development timetable, was voiced out in a summit held by several Clark stakeholders
and investors and that a manifesto urging the
government to consider Clark as the best and only
viable option to complement the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) was released in July 2013 which was made during a Clark Aviation Conference. Rep. Guiao thereafter relayed the following conclusions arrived at during the summit: 1) the need for the President to issue a policy statement on the role of Clark in national development; 2) the release of the fund committed by the Department of Transportation and Communications for the construction of a low-cost airline terminal; and 3) the inclusion of Clark in the first phase of the government´s projected mass railway system. After urging the government to immediately act on the matter, he thanked the Representatives from the Central Luzon bloc and the business chambers of Central and Northern Luzon for supporting his cause.
On motion of Rep. Lagdameo (M.), the Chair
recognized Rep. Señeres for his interpellation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Rep. Señeres inquired about the status of the
fund allocated by the previous Administration for the centennial exposition project in Clark, this as he disclosed that the money was taken from the government´s savings and part of which was first intended for the establishment of a consular office in Dubai to address the needs of the OFWs therein. He thereafter asked Rep. Guiao to include in his crusade the issue of said centennial project.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
(Continuation)
In closing, Rep. Señeres expressed hope that the
status of the said project would be looked into,
particularly the case that is now pending before the Supreme Court, through representations in writing by the Central Luzon leadership with the concerned agency to expedite its disposition.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.41,pp.8-9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Seneres. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H004;
rows.title_full: RECOGNIZING THE ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE PHILIPPINE SPECIAL OLYMPICS TEAM
rows.abstract:
Rep. Abueg first discussed the Special Olympics
founded by Ms. Eunice Kennedy Shriver in 1962 to
promote the just treatment of intellectually/
developmentally disadvantaged individuals and
develop their skills and competencies. He then adverted to the first Asia-Pacific Special
Olympics held in Australia in December 2013 and
commended the Philippine team for winning 99
medals. He stressed that the values they exhibited in their training and performance ennobled and inspired the entire nation. He urged the Body to adopt his House Resolution No. 705 in this regard; and manifested the inclusion of Reps. Franz E. Alvarez and Douglas S. Hagedorn as coauthors thereof. Rep. Abueg then named one by one the officials, athletes and coaches who comprised the Philippine contingent to the Asia Pacific Special Olympics. He also mentioned the names of his family members and
other guests who cheered the special athletes in Australia.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.42,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H069;
rows.mother_status: Pending With Rules (Included in OB on 2016-05-23)
rows.title_full: DEMOLITION OPERATIONS IN SITIO SAN ROQUE, QUEZON CITY
rows.title_short: Demolition In Sitio San Roque Agham Road
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Hicap expressed his
sentiments and affirmed the condemnation of Party-List Anakpawis on the violent demolition that happened in Sitio San Roque, Barangay Bagong Pag-Asa, Quezon City on Monday, January 27, 2014. He raised his concern on the lack of order of the Quezon City Police District (QCPD) and the demolition team that attacked the community and the absence of an official from the Office of the Quezon City Mayor or the QCPD who could have conducted a dialogue with the residents. Rep. Hicap opined that the recurring forceful demolitions in Sitio San Roque in preparation for the construction of commercial establishments, high-rise condominiums, residential townhouses, business hubs and structures for entertainment and recreation,
only indicate that money and business are the real interests of the local government of Quezon City and the PNoy government. He then asked for justice for the residents of Sitio San Roque whose rights have been allegedly violated because of the aggressive and unjust demolitions.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.42, p.9)
rows.status: Substituted by HB06446
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.
