rows.author: F102;
rows.title_full: PARTY LIST AKBAYAN'S INTERVENTION ON ENERGY ISSUES
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Walden F. Bello from Party-List Akbayan
who rose to address the recent developments in
the power industry, particularly the 4.5-peso per
kilowatt-hour rate hike imposed on its 53 million
consumers by the Manila Electric Company (Meralco). Stating that the concerns raised in the various public hearings conducted on the matter were related to deeper issues regarding the adequacy of the country´s energy regulatory system and the appropriateness of the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) of 2001, he then proposed the following steps that the government can take to tackle the Meralco
concern and solve the country´s power problem:
1) for the Department of Justice (DOJ)-Office for
Competition to release the results of its investigation on the charges of collusion in the recent rate price hike of Meralco that may show the possibility of collusion among key players in the energy industry; 2) the removal of Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) Chairperson Zenaida Ducut under the principle of command responsibility; 3) for the Members to oppose the use of the Malampaya Fund to reimburse Meralco for the P10-billion added cost it has passed on to its consumers; 4) to oppose the legislative
initiative providing the President with emergency
powers to address the energy crisis; and 5) for
the President to certify as urgent a legislative initiative to repeal, amend or replace the EPIRA.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Rep. Dela Cruz delved on the following issues:
the efforts being undertaken by Congress, the DOJ
and the Office of the President to end the monopoly in the energy sector and the collusion between the power producers and the industry players which include the Department of Energy (DOE) and the ERC; the role of the EPIRA in justifying the increase in the power generating costs; and Congress´ initiative to repeal or review the EPIRA. Rep. Dela Cruz pointed out that he has prepared amendments on the power generation component of the EPIRA and likewise suggested that the government actively exercise its regulatory functions over the energy sector. He also enjoined Rep. Bello to ask for copies of all the service contracts allotted by the
DOE on the exploration of the country´s oil and other natural energy resources. Rep. Bello then argued on the national security implications of the management of strategic national power energy utilities by multinational corporations
particularly the Chinese companies, considering the current political and military impasse between the Philippines and China. In view thereof, he pointed out that the government should also look into the NGCP energy service contract entered into by the national government with a Chinese company. Rep. Dela Cruz concurred therewith and argued on a proposed Resolution urging the comprehensive review of all the energy service contracts that are being entered into by the government. He thereafter commended Rep. Bello for his speech.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 42,p.9&10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G051;
rows.title_full: CELEBRATION OF THE 2014 WORLD HIJAB DAY
rows.abstract:
On the occasion of World Hijab Day that is being
celebrated on February 1 every year, Rep. Turabin- Hataman raised the issue of discrimination against Filipino Muslim women in employment, social status, religious beliefs, and social activities for their wearing of the hijab and niqab as veils and religious attire to cover their heads and face. She maintained that the wearing of hijab is required by the Holy
Quran to show modesty among women. Rep. Turabin-Hataman claimed that Party-List Anak Mindanao seeks to correct and address the misperception and prejudicial and discriminatory treatment of Muslim women wearing hijab. She stated that her group joins in the international cause and advocacy of wearing hijab on the occasion of
World Hijab Day and in line with her group´s priority measure or the Bill Against Discrimination on the Account of Ethnicity and Religious Belief. She thereafter expressed her gratitude to the Lady Legislators who had all dared themselves to wear hijab that day in celebration and support of the World Hijab Day. She maintained that the support of her female
colleagues has brought courage and strength to
women who are discriminated, oppressed, and persecuted against for simply choosing to wear hijab.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.42,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on MUSLIM AFFAIRS since 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H065;
rows.title_short: Peace And Order Problem In The Country
rows.abstract:
Rep. Atienza raised the issue of peace and order
conditions in the country. It is in this regard that he recalled of a meeting with Speaker Feliciano Belmonte Jr. last year regarding the proposal to file a resolution urging the presence in Congress of Secretary Manuel A. Roxas of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) and General Alan L. Purisima of the Philippine National Police (PNP)
to determine their concrete programs and solutions to the country´s peace and order problem. He stated that he is reiterating the proposal inasmuch as the Speaker and Members of Congress had also been concerned with the deteriorating peace and order situation.
He further stated that the failure of the DILG and the PNP to address the problem depicts the apparent lawlessness and unabated criminality in the streets and the ineptitude of law enforcement officials to secure the lives of ordinary Filipinos. He likewise argued on the proposed solutions to the peace and order problem such as the re-introduction of the
death penalty which, he said, cannot address the
peace and order problem and compensate for the
failure of law enforcement officials in maintaining an effective criminal justice system.
He thereafter urged Secretary Roxas and General
Purisima to resign from their posts if they cannot do their job well.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.43,p.16)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2014-02-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Bataoil, Erice and Dela Cruz. Referred to the Committee on Public Order and Safety.

rows.author: F069;
rows.title_full: REHABILITATION/RECONSTRUCTION OF ANGAT DAM
rows.abstract:
Upon Rep. Gunigundo´s motion, the Chair
recognized Rep. Ma. Victoria R. Sy-Alvarado from
the First District of Bulacan who rose to voice out the strong clamor of the Bulakeños for the
rehabilitation/reconstruction of the Angat Dam.
Among other issues, she expounded on the need to
implement immediately President Benigno S. Aquino
III´s commitment to rehabilitate Angat Dam, and the concern for the safety of the people of Bulacan and nearby provinces in the event of a 7.9-magnitude earthquake that might destroy the water reservoir. She also highlighted her concern and that of her constituents regarding the privatization and management by Korean Water of the Angat Dam, which she surmised will bring about changes in the water reservoir´s feasibility studies and rehabilitation plans that may result in undue and unjustifiable
delays in its rehabilitation. Rep. Sy-Alvarado expressed hope that the Angat Dam rehabilitation plan will soon be implemented to allay the fears and possible cost to lives, properties, and livelihood of the Bulakeños and those living in
nearby provinces. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.44,p.9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2014-02-11
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Bondoc. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G105;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. De Jesus brought the
issue of the privatization of Dr. Jose Fabella
Memorial Hospital to raise consciousness regarding the rights of marginalized women and children who will be adversely affected by the privatization of the public maternity hospital and its transfer to the DOH Compound.
She expressed apprehension on the following: 1)
the guidelines for the release and utilization of the Public-Private Partnership Strategic Support Fund (PPPSSF) for the modernization of DOH hospitals; 2) the issue of the modernization of Jose Reyes Medical Center, Fabella Hospital and San Lazaro Hospital; and 3) the negative impact of the privatization scheme on the original thrust of Fabella Hospital in delivering maternal health services to the
needy. She then called on her colleagues to resolve the crisis on women´s health service by preventing the privatization of public hospitals especially Fabella Hospital.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ZAMORA (R.)
Rep. Zamora initially discussed with Rep. De
Jesus the provision by the national government of
universal health care service to the needy, especially those in the remote countryside areas.
After she and her colleague agreed that public private partnership (PPP) projects mostly benefit the business sector, Rep. De Jesus said that she would file a resolution for the public disclosure of the details of the Fabella Hospital privatization plan. Rep. Zamora added that he would introduce a separate resolution for the renationalization of health facilities
and stressed the need for a universal health care system primarily concerned with the poor and underprivileged.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.44,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2014-02-11
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Zamora (R.). Referred to the appropriate Commitee (Rules)

rows.author: F122;
rows.title_short: Issues To Be Addressed By Congress
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz took the floor to enjoin his
colleagues to redouble their efforts to become the transformational institution the people expect them to be. He stated that for the past six months since the convening of the 16th Congress, the Members have witnessed the ebb and flow of being legislators and that for some reasons, they have allowed outside forces and special interest groups to stymie their
initiatives. In this regard, he proposed a list of issues and concerns which he hopes the Body could tackle and discuss, among which are the review of the 2015 budget in its entirety before the Executive comes out with its own budget proposal; amendments to the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA); codification of labor laws and their integration in the
Labor Code of the Philippines; review of the Magna Carta for Day Care Workers and other barangaybased employees; food self-sufficiency program of the government; and review of the National Shelter Program, and the retail trade, consumer protection and anti-trust laws.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 44,p.13)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-02-04)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Seneres and Atienza. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G093;
rows.title_short: 115th Anniversary Of The Phil - American War
rows.abstract:
Declaring that February 4, 2014 marks the 115th
Anniversary of the Philippine-American war, Rep.
Tinio described the said war to be the single
bloodiest and most brutal armed conflict that has ever taken place in the Philippines. Rep. Tinio narrated how the Philippine-American
war reflected the brutality of the Americans to the Filipinos and suggested that February 4 of every year be declared a special day in commemoration of our forefathers who sacrificed their lives in the forging of the modern Filipino nation. He then stressed that it is the government´s duty to seek justice, demand reparations and find closure for that chapter in the history of the Filipino people; and for the US government to take responsibility for the atrocities committed by its armed forces against
the Filipinos during the said war.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.44,p.13)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2014-02-11
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H073;
rows.title_full: RECLAIMING PUBLIC HEALTH CARE SERVICES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Paquiz spoke against the corporatization
and privatization of public health services in the guise of modernizing and reforming the health sector. Under this scheme, she said that the private-sector ways of doing business would prevail and that monetary goals would dominate health goals. She explained how this would thus result in service cuts especially in the local level where health services were devolved, with more focus on reducing service delivery costs rather than enhancing health care; and
less concern for improving the status and integrity of health workers. She called on her colleagues to consider a measure to re-nationalize devolved health care service delivery and to conduct an inquiry on
public-private partnership (PPP) projects involving public hospitals. She stressed that the government should reclaim public health services and never treat it as a business.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.47,p.9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2014-02-24
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Atienza, Dela Cruz and Ilagan. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G029;
rows.title_full: ON THE RECENT BUS ACCIDENT IN BONTOC, MOUNTAIN PROVINCE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dalog spoke about the recent vehicular
accident that occurred in Sitio Paggang, Talubin,
Bontoc, Mountain Province when a bus fell off a
ravine and resulted in the death of 14 passengers and injury of some 32 others. In behalf of the people of the province, he expressed sympathy to the families and friends of those who lost their lives, and commiserated with the injured. He likewise thanked the rescuers and volunteers from the nearby areas and
provinces. Considering that the Florida Bus Company lacked the necessary franchise to operate said route, Rep. Dalog asked Congress to conduct an immediate investigation on the operations and management of public utility bus companies and how the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) imposes stricter regulations and heavier penalties on erring bus companies. He likewise asked the Department of Public Works and Highways
(DPWH) and the Road Board to look into the
weather conditions and terrain in said areas as well as the road conditions therein, and if necessary, to install road signs, concrete barriers, parapets, guard rails and cat´s eye or tiger´s eye along mountainous roads to forestall road accidents and promote public safety. Since many of the wounded passengers were referred to Baguio City hospitals which are several
hours away from Bontoc, Mountain Province, he also appealed to the Department of Health (DOH) to favorably consider the upgrading of the Luis Hora Regional Memorial Hospital. He also asked the Members to investigate why the DOH has not
implemented existing laws pertinent thereto which
Congress had passed 17 years ago. Lastly, he urged the Department of Tourism (DOT) to look into ways to mitigate the effects of the particular vehicular accident to the country´s tourism.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.47,p.9&10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2014-02-24
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dela Cruz and manifestation by Dep. Speaker Padilla. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H072;
rows.title_full: STATE OF PHILIPPINE EDUCATION SECTOR
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Ridon discussed the
issue of tuition fee increase and its consequent and adverse effects to the parents and students in terms of tuition fee payments and the opportunity to study, and to the government that has not been able to exercise its authority to regulate tuition fee increases and to solve the shortage of government funding and support to tertiary education. Specifically, he explained how the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) has been remiss in its duty to comply with
the provisions of the law thus, becoming a
government agency merely approving petitions for
tuition fee hikes. He proposed to amend the provisions of the law, for the purpose of providing more equal access to education and to provide limitations on tuition fee increases. To ensure that the plight of the students that he had mentioned in his speech and the prejudicial circumstances of students from marginalized families will not be repeated, he hoped
that Congress will have to take immediate and
appropriate action on the matter. He urged his fellow Members to help in giving the Filipino youth access to reasonably priced and quality education. Thereafter, on motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair recognized Rep. Roy V. Señeres Sr. for his interpellation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Reps. Señeres and Ridon exchanged views on
why a lot of Filipinos do not have access to
education, mentioning poverty as one of the main
reasons therefor and the CHED´s approval of
petitions for tuition fee increase as just a small part of the equation. Rep. Señeres insisted on looking deeper into the reasons why there is widespread poverty in the country which deprives millions of Filipinos from pursuing college education.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.47,pp.10-11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2014-02-24
rows.remarks: Interpellation of Rep. Seneres. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H028;
rows.title_full: ALLEGED ANOMALIES AND IRREGULARITIES IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROJECTS OF THE NATIONAL IRRIGATION ADMINISTRATION
rows.title_short: Anomalies In The Implementation Of N I A Projects
rows.abstract:
Rep. Fortun spoke about corruption in government,
taking cognizance of the campaign slogan and
inaugural address of President Benigno S. Aquino III who promised reforms to rid government of corruption and to ensure transparency and accountability. He said that much as the present administration wants to do away with corruption, there are still government officials who openly disobey the President´s fight against corruption, such as certain officials of
the National Irrigation Authority (NIA) who are allegedly usurping the powers of the NIA administrator. He then called on the House to investigate the reported anomalies in the NIA-Caraga Regional Office.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,p.13-14)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2014-02-24
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Uy(J.), Dela Cruz, Seneres, Atienza and Romarate. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H081;
rows.title_full: ON THE CREDIBILITY AND COMPETENCE OF FORMER POLICE DIRECTOR LINA SARMIENTO IN RELATION TO HER APPOINTMENT TO THE HUMAN RIGHTS VICTIMS' CLAIMS BOARD
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zarate spoke about the President´s recent
appointment of former Police General Lina Castillo-Sarmiento as chairperson of the Human Rights Victims´ Claims Board, which he opined is an insensitive act and a dishonor to the memory and sacrifices made by the martial law victims. He maintained that the President should have appointed to the position a victim or a representative of the victims, instead of a
member of an agency that committed the most brutal human rights violations during the Marcos regime, and who, as the former director of the Philippine National Police Human Rights Affairs Office, was one of the apologists of the Arroyo administration. He said that as the people closely monitor the actions of the Aquino Claims Board, Congress should not allow the desecration of Republic Act No. 10368 which grants payments to martial law human rights victims.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,p.14)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2014-02-24
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F102;
rows.title_full: SAVING THE LAS PINAS AND PARANAQUE CULTURAL HABITAT AND ECO-TOURISM AREA
rows.title_short: Protection Of Las Pinas And Paranaque Cultural Habitat And Eco - Tourism Area
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello centered on the protection of the Las
Piñas-Parañaque Critical Habitat and Ecotourism
Area (LPPCHEA) located on the outskirts of Metro
Manila that has become the habitat for migratory
birds, host to a thick and diverse mangrove forest, and a natural barrier from storm surges and high tide, among others. He stressed that its crucial role in ensuring global ecological diversity has been given international
recognition, and then emphasized the need to raise awareness and public responsibility for its protection. He thereafter encouraged participants to the Nature and Bird Photography Workshop that Akbayan Party-List and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources would conduct, and enjoined his colleagues to support Akbayan´s proposed LPPCHEA Act of 2013.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,14)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2014-02-24
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H026;0000;
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE IMMEDIATE REHABILITATION OF THE SORSOGON NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL
rows.title_short: Rehabilitation Of Sorsogon National High School
rows.abstract:
Thereafter, on further motion of Rep. Abaya, the
Chair recognized Rep. Evelina G. Escudero from the First District of Sorsogon who spoke about a fire that razed the Sorsogon National High School building in Sorsogon City which she said destroyed many classrooms, offices and school equipment. She stated that the Sorsogon National High School is a historical landmark in Sorsogon City as it has retained its original architectural design, was used as a garrison
during the Japanese occupation and had produced
prominent political, religious and civic personalities. As such, she called on the Departments of Education (DepEd), and Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to provide immediate rehabilitation package to the Sorsogon National High School.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.49,p.14)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2014-02-24
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H025;
rows.title_short: Realignment Of P D A F
rows.abstract:
Rep. Erice dwelled on the lump-sum funds
handed out by Senator Jinggoy Estrada to the city
governments of Manila and Caloocan, and by Senator Nancy Binay to the National Housing Authority, which was an issue raised during a recent youth summit held in celebration of Caloocan´s 52nd anniversary as a city. This, as he lamented during the said occasion that he could not keep his campaign promises because the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) of the House Members was already abolished.
He recalled that it was made clear in the last
budget deliberations that the PDAF would be realigned to items of expenditures already existing in five agencies and that the Senate´s PDAF allocation would be reallocated to the unprogrammed funds of the General Appropriations Act. He then underscored the need for an explanation regarding the lump-sum funds being given out by the Senators especially since the Supreme Court has already ruled that the PDAF is unconstitutional. He thereafter asked for a detailed report on where the P4.8-billion Senate PDAF will go. Thereafter, the Chair recognized Rep. Amado S. Bagatsing for his interpellation.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.50,p.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-02-18
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Bagatsing and Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H013;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aragones, in commemoration of the 1986
EDSA Revolution which brought back the country´s
democracy and which became a shining example in
the international community, raised the issue of increasing violence and brutal killings of media people who pursue their profession in defense of the law, of democracy and of society. She averred that the culture of impunity persists
because only a few who seem to be beyond and outside the grasp of laws have been brought to justice for their heinous acts, thereby making the public´s dissatisfaction, helplessness and despair grow. She then appealed to the Members of Congress to help journalists by revisiting and evaluating the effectiveness of the laws and to see to it that the freedom of expression and information are still respected and protected in the country.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.52,pp.9&14)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-02-24
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Atienza, Seneres, Pagdilao and Mangudadatu. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.abstract:
Rep. Bagatsing spoke on the condition of Philippine sports in general and the government´s sports development policy program. As he cited the achievements of Mr. Michael Martinez - his passion for figure skating has captured the imagination of the whole world - the Gilas Basketball Team and Rep. Emmanuel D. Pacquiao, he averred that Philippine sports has a big role in unifying the country and has
given the chance to poor people to advance in life. He thereafter asked why the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (Pagcor) has been allocating only 2.5 percent of its gross income to the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) when the amount should have been 5 percent per Republic Act No. 6847. In closing, he stressed the importance of sports development particularly in public schools.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Belmonte (J.), Rep. Atienza inquired on the agency´s lack of funds to finance its numerous sports development programs, and stressed the need to train and give financial assistance to young and gifted young people in the fields of dance, arts or sports. He thereafter expressed support to Rep. Bagatsing´s effort to look into Pagcor´s failure to fully allocate 5 percent
of its gross income to the PSC, this as he pointed out that the amount is intended to support and sustain its numerous projects.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.52.(p.15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-02-25
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Atienza. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H081;
rows.title_short: Encampment Of Soldiers In Compostela Valley
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zarate brought to the attention of the Body
the wanton violation by the members of the Armed
Forces of the Philippines (AFP) of Republic Act
(RA) No. 7610 or the “Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act.” He described in particular, with the aid of a short video presentation, a recent incident involving the Philippine Army´s 25th Infantry Battalion which occupied a Department of Education (DepEd)- accredited learning center for indigenous children located in Mangayon, Compostela, Compostela Valley.
Citing several cases where schools and other
public facilities were being used for military purposes, he reiterated the call of child rights advocates and other human rights groups to the members of the AFP to stop the illegal practice of using public facilities, like schools, as command posts, barracks, detachments and supply depot in the conduct of its counterinsurgency operations. Finally, he said that he will file a resolution urging the proper House Committee to investigate said illegal actions that affect the rights and lives of children. He also asked his colleagues to support said investigation.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.52,p.19)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-02-25
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Acedillo. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules

rows.author: H065;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Atienza rose in commemoration of the 28th anniversary of the EDSA
People Power Revolution to bring awareness to
where people power had brought the Filipino people at present. He claimed that since February 25, 1986, the EDSA revolution had provided different meanings to numerous Filipinos that in the years to come, he is apprehensive that the real meaning of EDSA
people power revolution would be forgotten and
would no longer be appreciated. Rep. Atienza argued that the EDSA revolution and what it had imbued to the Filipinos should become an integral part of the history, culture, and
unique character of Filipinos and that it should be reinculcated as an inspiration to the present generation. However, inasmuch as there had been no institutional cultural programs to commemorate the EDSA revolution, he lamented that said historical event would still be far from becoming part of the unique character
and cultural consciousness of the Filipinos.
Further stressing the unifying effect of culture,
Rep. Atienza discussed how it was set aside after the EDSA Revolution. He said that what the succeeding administrations did was to promote foreign beliefs and practices, which only divided the nation as what the history of the Reproductive Health Act showed. To conclude, Rep. Atienza asked the nation to pray
for its leaders and heroes and to focus on the EDSA Revolution´s spirit of unity and progress rather than its personalities.
(House Journal No.52,p.19)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-02-25
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Seneres. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H069;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Hicap discussed the
worsening condition of the fisherfolk sector in the country, adding that Republic Act No. 8550 or the Fisheries Code of 1998 has failed to address its problems particularly the entry of foreign and local commercial fishing vessels in municipal fisheries and the privatization of fishing zones. He stressed that the sad plight of the local fishermen could be attributed
to the lack of a genuine land and fisheries reform program and a real national industrialization plan. He added that the problems of the fisheries sector would be further aggravated by the public-private partnership (PPP) reclamation projects of the government as it would dislocate the fishermen and would hamper their livelihood. He also stressed how the mining and energy sectors
have destroyed the country´s marine resources
and the fishing industry, and opined that the government´s “No-Build Zone, No-Dwell Zone” Policy is intended to protect its PPP program and not the small fisherfolks. Finally, he called for the abolition of the Fisheries Code of 1998; the termination of the National
Reclamation Plan; the stoppage of the “No-
Build, No-Dwell Zone” Policy; and the implementation of a genuine land and fisheries reform program as well as a true national industrialization plan.
(House Journal No.52,p.20)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-02-25
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F102;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello spoke about the rice crisis in the
country, particularly the issue of rice smuggling that
was brought about by the Philippine government´s
inclusion as a signatory to the 1995 Agreement on
Agriculture of the World Trade Organization allowing
the elimination of quantitative restrictions on agricultural
products except rice, and which the 10-year
period agreement was extended only up to 2012 and
now puts the country in a period of indeterminancy
insofar as rice quota extension agreement is concerned.
He added that the situation could have been
avoided had there been a closer coordination between
the Departments of Agriculture and Justice, and cautioned
that the country might be confronted with a
similar situation when the ASEAN Economic Community
becomes a reality in 2015. Finally, he stressed
the need for Malacañang to intensify the nation´s agricultural
policy to reinvigorate the agriculture industry,
promote the interests of the farmers, protect the
consumers, and control rice dumping by aggressive
international rice players.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 52,pp.20-21)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-02-25
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F093;
rows.title_short: Mass Movement Of Typhoon Yolanda Victims
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ilagan expressed her solidarity with the
victims of Typhoon Yolanda who trekked from
different areas of Eastern Visayas, collectively
calling themselves the People Surge Alliance for
Yolanda Victims, to air their urgent appeal for
solutions to the festering poverty and misery left by both the disastrous typhoon and the equally disastrous post-calamity management of the PNoy Administration. She underscored several relevant issues on the plight of the victims of natural calamities in Mindanao and Eastern Visayas from such typhoons as Sendong, Pablo and Yolanda, that the Gabriela Women´s Party-List supports and is now bringing to the attention of Congress for resolution: 1) the issue of injustice in the case of Christina Jose of Barog
Katawhan, who had been killed for exposing the
government´s corrupt management of relief goods
and the food and economic blockade by the 67th infantry battalion in Southern Mindanao; 2) the issue of negligence and indifference of government to the petition of People Surge to government agencies, such as the DSWD and the Office of the President, for a sustained governmental assistance to the victims
of Typhoon Yolanda in view of the absence of
food supplies and basic social services, livelihood programs and housing relocations; and 3) the absence of gender-disaggregated data in government´s disaster program database prejudicial to women victims in the government´s planning of rehabilitation programs. She thereafter expressed her appeal to the Members of Congress for their support to the just demands of the petitions by People Surge for the
victims of natural calamities.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 53,p.7)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-03)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: A016;
rows.abstract:
On further motion of Rep. Yap (S.), the Chair
recognized Rep. Belma A. Cabilao from the First
District of Zamboanga Sibugay who spoke about the
subject of annulment of marriage as provided for
under the Philippine Family Code. She noted that in the country, a couple whose marriage is
ecclesiastically annulled can get married again in the Catholic Church but the civil courts do not recognize such second marriage and deem it nonexistent and the parties thereto can still be found guilty according to the provisions of the Family Code, the Civil Code and the Penal Code. She expressed hope that the situation she spoke of would serve as an eye opener for the improvement of the present laws on legal
separation and annulment. In closing, Rep. Cabilao stated that there should be available relief when marriage becomes difficult and is no longer bearable, and reconciliation is next
to impossible.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.53,p.7)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-03)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H012;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Antonino-Nadres dealt on the women´s
struggle for their rights, especially the rights of pregnant women who should be given utmost care
and attention by giving due preference to address the problems on maternal and child care. She thereafter asked her colleagues to 1) join her in solving the problems of pregnant women not only in terms of prenatal care but of post natal care as well; 2) provide financial assistance to ensure that they receive proper
medical attention; 3) stop the privatization of Dr. Jose Fabella Memorial Hospital; and 4) work on legislative proposals to re-nationalize the devolved health services. She expressed her firm belief that there is no chance for the welfare of the country to improve unless the condition of women is improved.
(SOURCE: Journal No.53,p.8)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-03)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Commitee.

rows.author: H050;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Radaza delved on child pornography and
the operation of cyber prostitution. She said that it is unfortunate that said operations are being run by small and medium-scale operators under the guise of Internet services which she said is a “call center” of sorts that bridges helpless victims to paying patrons either for the purpose of pornography or prostitution.
She pointed out that in Lapu-Lapu City, the people are supporting her call to uplift the stature of women and children by engaging in activities that promote awareness and education on the responsible ways of using the Internet.
Taking into account the importance of educating
the public together with implementing the provisions of existing laws that protect the people from cybercrimes, Rep. Radaza asked Congress to study the possibility of incorporating in the school curriculum subjects that will touch on the responsible
use of Itechnology. She then ended her speech by encouraging the Members to listen to the plea of the women and children in their cry for help and their desire to regain the honor and dignity they deserve.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.53,p.8)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-03)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H052;
rows.title_short: Gender And Development ( G A D ) Fund
rows.abstract:
Rep. Gerona-Robredo stressed the need to value
and help women, specifically the marginalized and
silent ones who continue to struggle w/ poverty, illiteracy, sexual harassment, discrimination, and trafficking in the poorest of the regions of the country. She then asked national government agencies and local government units (LGUs) to implement the following: Republic Act (RA) No. 9710 (Magna Carta of Women) on allocating certain percentages of their budgets, official development assistance, and soft loans for gender and development (GAD) projects; and the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DIlG) circular on publicly disclosing GAD budgets. She informed the Body of how her constituency from Naga City had been applying the intent and spirit of these measures.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.53,p.8)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-03)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G051;
rows.title_short: Role Of Women In Obtaining Peace In Mindanao
rows.abstract:
Recognized next by the Chair, Rep. Sitti Djalia
A. Turabin-Hataman from AMIN Party-List rose on
behalf of the Moro, Christian, and indigenous women in Mindanao. Speaking in a mix of Filipino and English, she initially spoke of the past and present issues of poverty, armed conflict, lack of education, smuggling, trafficking, and issues that have plagued the region. She subsequently stressed, however, that Mindanaoan women will not allow this situation to continue. She informed the Body of positions held as well as roles played by individual women and women´s groups in advancing peace, in legislative and executive work in regional and national offices,
and in training and empowering the women sector.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.53,p.9)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-03)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Commitee.

rows.author: H013;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in a mix of English and Filipino, Rep.
Aragones initially presented before the Body a
shampoo commercial showing discrimination against
women all over the world which originated from the Philippines that took the globe by storm and went viral in the Internet. She lamented that women in various endeavors have suffered from different kinds of biases, criticisms and inequalities on the belief that men are more efficient and skilled. She called on her lady colleagues to educate and empower the people
against gender stereotypes because women are also
capable of being successful in their chosen careers and are crucial in addressing issues like poverty. She also urged them to support and institutionalize economic empowerment initiatives.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.53,p.9)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-03)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H026;
rows.title_short: Human Trafficking In Typhoon Yolanda Affected Areas
rows.abstract:
Rep. Escudero called attention to the issue of
human trafficking which she said is an incidental
effect of natural calamities because their victims are
more vulnerable to the evil designs of human
trafficking syndicates. She called on her colleagues
and the government agencies concerned to do their
share in promoting awareness against this scheme,
particularly to the people living in the areas affected
by Typhoon Yolanda.
She enumerated the salient features of RA No.
10364 or the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons
Act of 2012, and then encouraged the people to be
vigilant so they will not become victims of human
trafficking and prevent the continuance of pernicious
activities of syndicates.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.53,p.9)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-03)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H016;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Joseph “Ace” H. Durano, Rep. Catherine Barcelona-
Reyes, M.D. spoke about the joint efforts of certain government agencies that she initiated in September 2013 that led to the dismantling of illegal Chinese mining companies in the First District of Camarines Norte. She stressed that the pillage of the country´s mineral wealth is an insult to the integrity and dignity of the Filipino people, and could create damage and
losses to the government through environmental
degradation, job deprivation and revenue loss.
While she stressed that the illegal mining cleanup operation in the province is still ongoing and would put to test the mettle and commitment of said agencies in fighting corrupt elements, she thanked Justice Secretary Leila De Lima for her support and assistance on the matter.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.54,p.19)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-04)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G095;
rows.abstract:
Upon Rep. Defensor´s motion, the Chair
recognized Rep. Reynaldo V. Umali from the Second
District of Oriental Mindoro who spoke about the
need for judicial reform as he cited several instances wherein the Supreme Court (SC) had apparently usurped the powers of its coequal branches. He mentioned, among others, the cases where the High Tribunal 1) declared as unconstitutional the impeachment cases filed in the House against former Chief Justice Hilario Davide; 2) intervened in the jurisdiction of the House of Representatives Electoral Tribunal (HRET) as the sole judge of election controversies; 3) and usurped the prosecutorial
powers of the Executive Department when it directed public prosecutor to prosecute individuals related to the improper utilization of the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF). Rep. Umali (R.) also adverted to several cases where the SC violated the principle of immutability of final judgments which is the basic principle that supports the stability of a judicial system, as well as the social, economic and political ordering of society and betrayal of public trust. In arguing on the doctrine of immutability of final decision and the
repeated reversal or flip-flopping of SC decisions, Rep. Umali adverted to the public position of Justice Brion and journalist Marites Danguilan-Vitug who emphasized that without the finality and executory ruling by the SC in its decisions, the latter had established that judgments can no longer achieve finality in the country and eroded the people´s confidence in the rule of law. In view thereof, Rep. Umali reiterated his advocacy to secure justice for the people and bring back integrity in the judiciary by urging his colleagues to take the corresponding actions against judicial “flip-flopping” and bullying, judicial favoritism and cronyism, and betrayal of public trust in encroaching on the powers of a coequal branch of
government and allocating “pork barrel” in the
judiciary in the form of the judicial development
fund (JDF). He explained that the unprecedented
action of the Supreme Court in the aforementioned
cases had caused apprehension not only in the halls of Congress but also among the public, and is further eroding the country´s judicial and political systems. (Continuation) Rep. Umali called upon the Members of Congress not to allow the continuing emasculation of the Constitution and not to remain silent and subservient to the excesses of the judiciary; and called upon similar-minded advocates for judicial reform and constitutional integrity to join him in his
crusade and advocacy. (SOURCE: House Journal No.54,pp.19 & 20)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-04)
rows.remarks: Suspended...

rows.author: G017;
rows.abstract:
In celebration of the women´s month, Rep.
Calixto-Rubiano delved on the life of Ms. Jessica
Macabare Cox Chamberlain to serve as an inspiration to millions of people around the world because of her courage and perseverance when she was born without arms as a result of a rare birth defect but has learned to live her life using her feet. She then relayed Jessica´s various achievements since childhood until she pursued her degree in Psychology at the University of Arizona and became the first armless person to earn a black belt in the
American Taekwondo Association. She added that
Jessica´s most famous accomplishment was learning
how to fly, thus receiving recognition from the
Guinness Book of World Record as the first armless person in aviation history to earn a pilot´s certificate. Rep. Calixto-Rubiano underscored that in fulfilling her dream to launch a career as a motivational speaker and an advocate for the disabled, Jessica has traveled to more than 20 countries sharing her inspirational story and experiences. She then mentioned some of Jessica´s numerous international awards and accolades.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 54,pp.21-22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-03-04
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G105;
rows.abstract:
In the spirit of the worldwide and yearly celebration of the International Women´s Day, Rep. De Jesus stressed in Filipino her Party-List´s concern for the plight of the marginalized women and children in the country. Specifically, she dwelled on the failure of
the government to provide adequate social and health services to the public, mentioning in detail the planned privatization through the public-private partnership (PPP) schemes of the Dr. Jose Fabella Memorial Hospital and the Philippine Orthopedic Center, and its possible negative implications on the poor. She then read into the records the unity statement initiated by the Makabayan Coalition in the House and supported by the Minority Bloc, opposing the
privatization of the two hospitals and the selling of health services. She also urged her colleagues to join the Legislators United for Service-Oriented Government or LUSOG hospitals and help promote the welfare and rights of the people.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.54, pp.26-28)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-05)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Atienza, Paquiz, Dela Cruz and Rodriguez (R.). Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H058;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tan adverted to media reports on a mysterious skin disease spreading in Pangasinan and asked why the diagnoses of the provincial health officer and of a private dermatologist differed as regards one of the alleged victims thereof. As she presented a video showing an interview on the said dermatologist, Rep. Tan asked for the basis of the provincial health officer´s diagnosis and why the health authorities acted only now. She stated that the DOH should explain the lapses in health protocol especially the implementation scheme of the National Leprosy Control Program. She then called on Congress to investigate the present delivery of health services in the country, to
recommend a more efficient implementation of appropriate measures, and to provide budgetary support to the DOH to improve health services for the vulnerable sectors of society.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. CHIPECO
Debating in Filipino, Reps. Chipeco and Tan (A.)
discussed the details and adverse effects of the so-called skin disease pyoderma gangrenosum and
agreed that Congress should investigate the matter particularly the implementation of the National Leprosy Control Program in order to combat said disease.  INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAQUIZ Reps. Paquiz and Tan (A.) discussed the quality of health care delivery system in the country as both Members agreed that Congress should investigate the present system to address the health concerns of the people, especially the poor. (SOURCE: House Journal No.54,p.28)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-05)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Chipeco and Paquiz. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H056;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Suansing focused on the promotion of
women development in the country by citing several constitutional provisions, laws, and congressional as well as executive efforts in recognizing, enhancing and sustaining the role of women in society. She however noted the continuous setbacks that women have suffered from, particularly in the fields of employment,
education, health, and public affairs because
of lower job skill categories, multiple responsibilities, sexual exploitation, and limited access to credit, training and technology especially for women engaged in agricultural activities, among others. She
thereupon called on her colleagues to support the
numerous bills pending in the House that aim to
promote gender equality and women development,
with the goals of the Philippine Plan for Gender Responsive Development for the years 1995 to 2025 as guide in the crafting of such measures.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.54,p.30)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-05)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H068;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in commemoration of the first death
anniversary of Dexter Condez, a Boracay Ati tribe
leader who fought for the rights of his tribe, Rep. Gutierrez dwelled on the issue of the nonresolution of the former´s murder case despite the identification of his assailant.
He also raised his concern over the displacement
of the Atis in Boracay due to the establishment of commercial centers in their ancestral lands, and the intimidation and harassment received by said tribal group. He then urged the Members to extend respect and fairness to the Atis.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.54,p.30)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-05)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F057;
rows.title_full: STATE OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Thereafter, on motion of Rep. Tugna, the Chair
recognized Rep. Rodriguez (R.) who spoke on the
status and difficulties of the micro-small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) financing in the Philippines to access credits from commercial and local financial institutions. He also pointed out that MSMEs´ lack of access to new technology, innovation, and research, inadequate technological competence, limited resources,
and small size contribute to their low productivity. To address the plight of the MSMEs, Rep. Rodriguez proposed the revision of Republic Act (RA) No. 9501 or the Magna Carta for MSMEs, particularly on the definition of the term “loan portfolio,” and the sanctions on noncompliance to the mandatory allocation of loans. After citing the salient provisions
of the resolution of the Congressional Oversight
Committee on MSMEs Development issued
during the 15th Congress, he urged the Members to
support the MSMEs through the proper implementation of the Magna Carta for MSMEs, as well as to convene the Oversight Committee for said law to help improve the lives of poor Filipinos. (SOURCE: House Journal No.54,pp.30-32)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SMALL BUSINESS & ENTREPRENEURSHIP DEVELOPMENT since 2014-10-29
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

referrals.committee: MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT

rows.abstract:
Rep. Bagatsing categorically denied a statement
made by Mr. Dennis Cunanan through a television
news report last Wednesday, March 5, 2014, alleging that Rep. Bagatsing allocated the amount of P8 million out of his Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) to the Masaganang Ani Foundation through the Technological Resource Center (TRC)from 2005 to 2008. He expressed hope that Mr. Cunanan would correct his sworn affidavit as well as
clarify the issue through a public statement.
(SOURCE: Journal No.55,pp.9-10)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-10)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H073;
rows.title_short: Government Employees Affected By Typhoon Yolanda
rows.abstract:
Rep. Paquiz from Ang Nars Party-List presented
before the Body the deplorable situation of government employees affected by Typhoon Yolanda, the Zamboanga crisis, and the Bohol and Cebu earthquakes, who despite being victims of calamities themselves were required to immediately report back to work because of the vital services that they have to perform under difficult and dangerous circumstances. She also described the housing loan scheme made available to such civil servants, and how they are always the last to receive relief assistance and government support even as they are expected to render quality public service and rebuild the communities they serve. She called on Congress to exercise its power of the purse in ensuring that funds are provided for the rehabilitation and rebuilding of the areas affected by said tragedies, including those intended for the civil
servants. After commending the various groups who
extended relief efforts and counseling to affected civil servants and their families, she reminded the Executive department and those involved in rehabilitation efforts that government employees are human beings, too, who deserve government support. (SOURCE: House Journal No.55,p.10)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-10)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H072;0000;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Ridon delved on the
anomalies and corruption hounding the completion of projects and allocation of funds for the rehabilitation of Typhoon Yolanda victims. He likewise talked about the group People Surge´s clamor for help and demand for immediate government action when they marched to Malacañang and the seeming inaction by the PNoy Administration on the matter.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. RODRIGUEZ (R.)
Rep. Rodriguez initially inquired whether Rep.
Ridon could show proof that the bunkhouses built for the Yolanda victims were overpriced or might be substandard in quality. This, as he revealed that based on his experience in Cagayan de Oro City when Typhoon Sendong struck the province, the bunkhouses that were constructed by volunteer contractors were properly built using just a meager budget and with no allegations of overpricing and substandard quality. Refuting his colleague´s claims, Rep. Rodriguez argued that a Member should promptly support a speech with evidence and not hearsay such as a Cabinet Secretary´s media statement that the bunkhouses
might not be overpriced but substandard. He
pointed out that as a United Nations adviser on disaster reduction, he could vouch for the good quality of the bunkhouses; President Aquino´s several visits to the affected areas; the provision of food, shelter, health services, and livelihood by various agencies and departments; and the victims´ requests not for cash dole out but for empowerment and rehabilitation.
He disagreed with Rep. Ridon´s view that the
Conditional Cash Transfer Program was a dole out
program, saying that its beneficiaries were required to do something in return for the funds they receive from the government.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. COLMENARES
Reps. Colmenares and Ridon discussed on the issue
of overpriced and substandard bunkhouses in
Tacloban City and Leyte that were built for the victims of Typoon Yolanda. Both Members exchanged views on the statements made by DPWH Secretary Rogelio Singson and the assessment of the United Nations with regard to the specifications of the overpriced and substandard
bunkhouses. Rep. Ridon then proposed that the government should scrap the no-build zone policy, provide a sustained relief distribution program and funding for agricultural rehabilitation, and pull out foreign troops
in the area in order to really address the problems of calamity victims.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ERICE
Reps. Erice and Ridon delved on the statements
made by the DPWH Secretary regarding the building
of overpriced and substandard bunkhouses, with the former arguing that there was no anomaly in the transactions considering that the bunkhouses were donated to the government and no payment was
made to the contractors.
INTERPELLATION OF DEPUTY SPEAKER APOSTOL
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Apostol refuted Rep. Ridon´s allegation that the bunkhouses constructed in Samar and Leyte were substandard as he stressed that it was not the proper time to make criticisms but to help the victims of Typhoon Yolanda.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Rep. Dela Cruz sought clarification in Filipino
the assessment made by the United Nations with respect to government´s response to the victims of and the areas affected by natural calamities, particularly in Eastern Visayas, as well as Finance Secretary Cesar Purisima´s statement as published in the Manila Times that the coconut industry would no longer be revived in the said region. He thereafter expressed support to a resolution summoning concerned government
officials to explain their respective rehabilitation plans. (SOURCE: House Journal No. 55,pp.19-20)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-03-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Rodriguez(R.), Colmenares, Erice, Apostol and Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate Committee (Rules)

rows.author: H026;
rows.title_short: Role Of Women In Nation Building
rows.abstract:
Rep. Escudero, in emphasizing the important role
of Filipino women in community development and
nation-building, explained that through participation in various significant endeavors in the community, Filipino women are able to make indelible contributions to society. She maintained however that the more important contribution they can make is by re-living their traditional role as Filipinas, wives, and
mothers - the veritable Ilaw ng Tahanan who has
provided the necessary strength and guidance to
every Filipino family. She thereafter appealed to every Filipino woman to choose to prioritize the interests and well-being of her family over other endeavors to help sustain a better Philippine society.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 55,p.29)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-03-11
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H081;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zarate spoke of the bravery of his Moro
brothers and sisters in fighting for their rights and freedoms and the month of March being memorable to them as they commemorate 1) the Bud Daju Day in remembrance of the more than a thousand Moro men, women and children who resisted foreign occupation but instead were massacred by American troops inside the crater of Mount Daju; and 2) the Bangsamoro Freedom Day in remembrance of the infamous Jabiddah massacre where at least 68 Moro youth of mostly Tausug and Sama descent were killed. To date, Rep. Zarate stated that instead of rectifying past mistakes, attacks against the rights of the Moro people still continue and apparently being left muted in the process, following the signing of the annexes to the Framework Agreement on the
Bangsamoro. He thereafter challenged the Aquino government to 1) reverse and stop the so-called “war on terror” policy adopted by the previous administration and lift the “state of lawlessness” policy in Basilan; and 2) revoke Memorandum Circular No. 40 that justifies
the conduct of unbridled police and military
saturation drives and arbitrary arrest of Moro
civilians on false charges of being members of the Abu Sayyaf group. Finally, he called on his
colleagues to fight for the defense& advancement
of the rights of the Moro people. (SOURCE: House Journal No.55,p.30)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-03-11
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F012;
rows.title_short: Obeyance Of The Rule Of Law
rows.abstract:
Rep. Barzaga enumerated the events surrounding
the Supreme Court´s (SC) final and executory
decision to cancel the certificate of candidacy of Rep. Regina Ongsiako Reyes for the position of
Representative of the Lone District of Marinduque. He decried her continued defiance of the same and the Body´s continued grant to her of the rights and privileges which should have accrued to her political opponent, Mr. Lord Allan Velasco. They were nullifying the powers of the Commission on Elections and Supreme Court, he opined, and trifling with the system of checks and balances and the separation of the three branches of government. He asked the Members to respect and obey the rule of law and the supremacy of the Constitution, and to
recognize Mr. Velasco as the district´s legitimate Representative.  
SOURCE: House Journal No.55,pp30-32)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-11)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Leachon, Umali(R.), Tiangco and Sato. Manifestation by Rep. Dela Cruz (Re:OFWs). Referred to the appropriate Commitee.

rows.abstract:
On behalf of the indigenous peoples (IPs) affected by mining operations, Rep. Padilla rose to condemn Republic Act (RA) No. 7942 or the Mining Act of 1995. He opined that 19 years since it took effect, RA No. 7942 had failed to manage the country´s mineral resources but instead, had legalized the plunder of the country´s national patrimony in view of the many problems and issues hounding the law, such as allowing 100% ownership of minerals by foreign entities, exploiting the protection and conservation of the country´s natural resources, and stepping on the IPs´ right to self determination on how to best use the resources within their ancestral domain. He added that even the National Statistical Coordination
Board has indicated that the contribution of the
mining industry to the country´s gross domestic
product (GDP) is very low. In this regard, Rep. Padilla enjoined his colleagues to establish more “No-Go Mining Zones,” assess the implementation of RA No. 7942, enact a
Philippine mineral resources law, and support a
measure calling for an alternative minerals management system. (SOURCE: House Journal No.55,p.44)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-03-12
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: A014;
rows.title_short: Update Report On C A R P
rows.abstract:
In view of the imminent expiration of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program Extension with Reforms (CARPER) Act on June 30, 2014, Rep.
Bichara stressed the need for the House to first ensure that the program´s objectives had been met and that its provisions had been effective before crafting another law for agrarian reform purposes. He thereafter asked the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) and the Department of Agriculture (DA) to submit to Congress a full report on the following: 1) the total land area covered and distributed to agrarian reform
beneficiaries (ARBs); 2) the percentage of said lands that are still being used or were sold; 3) the total identified lands still subject to CARP until and after June 30, 2014; 4) a comparative data on food production before and after the program´s implementation; 5) the current status of ARBs and CARPER implementation; and 6) the reasons why DAR would not be able to finish its job by June 2014.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
In his interpellation, Rep. Dela Cruz thanked
Rep. Bichara for explaining that his speech does not oppose the extension of the CARPER Act, but only stresses the point that it should not be extended unless the DAR presents to Congress a full report on the status of the 26-year old program. Rep. Bichara expressed concern that most of the beneficiaries had already sold their lands because they are no longer interested in farming, or have failed to make payments
thereon.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. RODRIGUEZ (R.)
Recognized by the Chair, Reps. Rufus B. Rodriguez
and Bichara´s debate centered on the need,
through the DAR, to first evaluate the CARPER Act
before crafting another law that would extend its life, given the huge number of distributed lands that have remained unproductive due to lack of support programs, as well as the need to first determine whether the intention of improving the lives of the beneficiaries has been achieved. Rep. Rodriguez (R.) stressed that the reason for the noncompletion of land distribution is the lack of appropriate funds that would support the program. He further pointed out that the granting of lands have
improved the lives of the beneficiaries in Mindanao and that there are still others who ought to receive the same which therefore justifies the extension of the CARP for another five years. He also said that foreigners
must not have land in the country if the Filipino
people themselves will not have their own. In reply, Rep. Bichara said that agrarian reform is
not merely a question of land distribution but the economic benefit derived from it. He emphasized that he is not opposed to the extension of the CARP but he needs the data that would substantiate the need for its extension since the DAR was not able to finish its work in the last five years and has yet to provide the House with the required accomplishment report. (SOURCE: House Journal No.55, pp.44-45)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-12)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Dela Cruz and Rodriguez (R.) Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz proposed in his speech that Congress determine and implement the right mix of feasible and progressive policies and legislations necessary to nation-building for the country to attain economic growth and equity particularly in light of a highly contentious global economy and the move to propose amendments to the economic provisions of
the 1987 Constitution. While he welcomes the decision of Speaker Feliciano Belmonte Jr. to defer until after the Congress recess, the discussion on Charter change, he would like that a congressional inquiry be conducted first to supplant the relevant measures regarding unfair trade and anticompetitive practices that had been filed before Congress, and to determine
the extent of several questionable arrangements and contracts entered into by the government that virtually provides foreign ownership of vital and critical industries in the power and telecommunications, housing, business, trade, and infrastructure sectors. He maintained that a congressional inquiry on these issues and pertaining to foreign ownership of the country´s vital industries and resources would help
determine how the same have become prejudicial to
the country´s economic growth and development, as
well as provide remedial legislative measures
thereon.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Rep. Señeres discussed with Rep. Dela Cruz the
appalling effects on the national coffers of the 90% of revenues of the Malampaya Fund accruing to multinational companies like Shell and Chevron and the foreign ownership of vital Philippine industries that is deemed prejudicial to the interests of the country and the 10 million overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) who contribute $22-billion worth of revenues annually
to the country´s economy. They also tackled the
issue of non-Filipino business personalities or Filipino partners who represent the interests of foreign businesses in the country and whether they will be summoned in a congressional inquiry.
Reps. Señeres and Dela Cruz both agreed that an
appropriate committee should conduct an inquiry in aid of legislation and even oversight on the following matters: 1) the participation of foreign investors in the so-called commanding heights of the economy beginning with the exploration of natural resources starting with Malampaya; and 2) the operations of such vital sectors as power, telecommunications, housing, transportation and railways, among others. Rep. Dela Cruz then stated that he will soon file
a Resolution to summon business tycoons Manny V.
Pangilinan, Andrew Tan, the Gokongweis and the
Ayalas, among others, to shed light on their economic activities that are considered basic services by nature and part of the commanding heights of the economy.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BATOCABE
Reps. Batocabe and Dela Cruz discussed how the
government can contain the unfair trade and anticompetitive practices going on in the country; the extent of control of foreigners over corporations that dominate the supposed commanding heights of the economy which at the same time, provide basic services to the people; and the possible enactment of an Anti-Trust Law to be able to determine how foreign ownership should be directed for the good of the public. (SOURCE: House Journal No.55,pp.48-49)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-03-12)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Seneres and Batocabe. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H025;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Erice discussed the economic impact in the
country of the truck ban being imposed by the City of Manila. He pointed out that because of the hasty implementation of an ordinance imposing the truck ban, the transportation of goods within the country has been disrupted thus preventing local businesses from abiding with their international shipping contracts which resulted in huge losses for the economy and risks in the employment of thousands of workers. He stated that since the implementation of the truck ban in the City of Manila, the Bureau of
Customs has reported a 25% decrease in their
revenue collection and that foreign businesses have expressed alarm on the matter. He stressed that the city government of Manila should first exhaust all the possibilities to improve traffic in their area and should not pass ordinances that will affect the welfare of its neighboring cities. He then called on the Committees on Local
Government, and Metro Manila Development to
investigate the matter. He also enjoined his
colleagues to pass House Bill No. 712 creating the Metro Manila Regional Administration to be vested with political and legislative powers to enable it to effectively solve all the issues spawned by a burgeoning metropolis.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 56,p.35)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-05
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H073;
rows.abstract:
In commemoration of Labor Day, Rep. Paquiz
brought to the attention of the Body the cry of the laborers, both from the private and public sectors, who are denied of decent pay for decent work and their perennial problem on the lack of security of tenure and the creeping disintegration of their right to organize.
She thereafter focused on the mandate of the
Civil Service Commission (CSC) to protect and
strengthen the human resources of the government;
underscored the need to strengthen the civil service and called on her colleagues to stop labor contractualization and all forms of precarious work arrangements in the public sector by passing the Security of Tenure Bill and the proposed Civil Service Code.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
... Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr. discussed with Rep. Paquiz how labor contractualization both in the public and private sectors has allowed the rich to become richer to the detriment of the poor working class. They agreed on the need to protect the labor force by immediately crafting laws that will address this concern.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.56,pp.35-36)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-05
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F035;
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Gunigundo...criticized the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) for requiring all marginal income earners (MIE), such as the farmers, small retail store owners, and tricycle drivers and operators, to register with the bureau or face the threat of fines and business closure if they fail to do so. Among other
arguments, he said that the BIR cannot derive
revenues from the MIEs as they are even considered income tax exempt under the Barangay Micro Business Enterprises Law. He also mentioned an article tackling the tax liability of Dunkin Donuts. Rep. Gunigundo enjoined his colleagues to unite and help recall the said BIR regulations and also asked the Committee on Ways and Means to conduct an inquiry on the matter.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PADILLA
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Carlos M.
Padilla requested Rep. Gunigundo to shed light on
the incorrect income tax assessment of Dunkin
Donuts which the BIR allowed to be re-examined but failed to disclose its actual tax obligations for 2007. Rep. Padilla then suggested that the congressional
inquiry to be conducted on the issue likewise include
a mining company from Nueva Vizcaya which he
surmised was not being properly assessed for its tax
dues.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-05
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Padilla. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G093;
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Antonio L. Tinio from Party-List ACT TEACHERS ... condemned theEnhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) which the governments of the United States (US) and the Philippines recently signed. He then surmised that the delay in the release of the content of the EDCA to the public was part of a carefully planned media strategy intended to shield US President Barack Obama from embarrassment during his state visit to the country. He claimed that the Philippine government and its designated spokespersons have continued to peddle partial truths and outright lies on the content of the agreement such as allowing US military access to agreed locations, effectivity of the agreement,
constitutional prohibition on nuclear weapons in
Philippine territory, and control over the
facilities used, among others. He pointed out that President Benigno S. Aquino III had surrendered Philippine sovereignty to the US government as the core of the EDCA is to establish military bases in the country. After citing other provisions of the agreement like the tax-free use of utilities, operation of their
own telecommunication system, and the granting of
extra-territoriality to US forces, including US
contractors in the Philippines, Rep. Tinio referred to the constitutional provision requiring a treaty to be concurred in by the House and the Senate, or duly ratified by a majority of the votes cast by the people in a national referendum on the establishment of
foreign military bases, and recognized as a treaty by the other contracting State. He concluded that the Filipino people should not accept the fiction being foisted by Malacañang to Congress and the public, and asked the people to reject EDCA and to hold President Aquino accountable for his action.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BIAZON
Rep. Biazon aired his concern on the need for
EDCA and the issue of its constitutionality.
Rep. Biazon then moved that the matter be
referred to a joint hearing of the Committees on
Foreign Affairs, National Defense and Security, and such other committees that may be involved in
determining whether or not the Philippines should
adopt EDCA. QUERY FROM THE CHAIR The Chair inquired why the matter was being referred to a House committee as he argued that the Body has no jurisdiction over treaty matters.
REMARKS OF REP. BIAZON Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Biazon said that their constituents need to be clarified on the EDCA because it is of national significance. While the Senate is mandated to concur in the agreement, he under scored that the House, being the originator
of any appropriations bill, needs to examine whether or not public funds are needed to implement the agreement. REMARKS OF REP. TINIO
The Chair then recognized Rep. Tinio who
remarked that even as the President is empowered to negotiate and enter into treaties, the House may allow inquiries and investigations to decide whether such agreement needs ratification and plebiscite since the 1987 Phil. Constitution has set a high standard concerning the re-entry of foreign troops and bases into the country after 1991. He then agreed to the motion of Rep. Biazon. REMARKS OF REP. BIAZON Rep. Biazon reiterated his motion, adding that the issue on EDCA should be clarified before the public and that there are questions requiring a response from the House. (SOURCE: House Journal No.57,pp.42-44)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-14
rows.remarks: Interpellation and Remards by Rep. Biazon. Referred to the Committee on Rules
