rows.author: F100;
rows.title_short: Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement ( E D C A )
rows.abstract:
Rep. Colmenares spoke in opposition to the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA)
which the Philippines and United States governments recently signed in contravention of the requirements of the Constitution regarding the participation of both Houses of Congress and the people in its ratification.... the Chair thereafter allowed Rep. Colmenares to continue
with his speech wherein the latter further argued
that the EDCA violates certain constitutional
provisions concerning the establishment of military bases thereby violating the nation´s sovereignty. He claimed that the argument used by the government that the EDCA does not comply with the criteria defining military bases, namely, territoriality, exclusivity, and ownership, is without legal basis because the
provisions of the EDCA, specifically paragraph 1,
Article III, provide for the activities and functions of a military base and establishment of permanent buildings. Rep. Colmenares then enumerated the provisions of the EDCA which he deemed as favorable to the United States, including among others, the operational control of agreed locations; exclusive and unencumbered
right to use and remove prepositioned material for emergency or war; denial of access to base areas if inconsistent with operational and security requirements; and exemption from taxes and fees. He however stressed that said provisions violated the sovereignty of the Philippines as well as its laws such as those on procurement, local government, and granting of inspection and police powers to government agencies. He also remarked that the prohibition against nuclear arms was confusing and the 1987 Constitution disallowed foreign military bases in the country after the expiration of the US-RP
Military Bases Agreement. Finally, he noted that that there was no mention in EDCA of Americans defending the country against any Chinese incursion of the Scarborough Shoal and Spratly Islands. INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Reps. Señeres and Colmenares discussed the issue
of increased US military presence in the Philippines and its effects on the nation´s sovereignty, commercial and economic values, and the possible attraction into the country of America´s enemies. This, as the former cited the ongoing activities of China against the Philippines. They also tackled the hegemonic tendencies of both the US and mainland China, with Rep. Colmenares airing the view that it is more appropriate to bring the Philippine-China issue in the West Philippine Sea to an international tribunal than for the Philippines
to seek US aid on the matter. In addition, the
Members dealt with the diplomatic undertones of the US government´s pronouncements. In closing, Rep. Señeres reminded his colleagues to consider not only the military dimension of EDCA but its economic implications as well. Meanwhile, Rep. Colmenares called on Congress to take up the cudgels for the Filipino people and assert the national sovereignty against US intrusion....  Reps. Dela Cruz and Colmenares exchanged views on the unconstitutionality of the EDCA which
the latter stressed does not merely implement the
provisions of the Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) and
the Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA). Rep. Colmenares explained that certain provisions in the EDCA, specifically pertaining to venues for settling disputes, prepositioning of war material, and deployment of troops are not found in the VFA; and the MDT cannot be used as the basis of an executive agreement to justify the lawful presence of American military personnel in the country. He opined that the EDCA should be considered a treaty to be considered
constitutional. With regard to the extent of applicability of the EDCA, Rep. Colmenares explained that the agreement is a self-perpetuating “treaty” until it is terminated
by both governments. Considering that the
EDCA does not conform with the requisites of the
Constitution requiring a treaty to be also recognized by the United States, the concurrence of the Philippine Senate, and a referendum or plebiscite for ratification if Congress so requires, the EDCA then becomes a contravention of the 1987 Constitution. Reps. Colmenares and Dela Cruz discussed in Filipino how the EDCA practically makes the Philippines a military base as it allows the US to use any public and private land to store, manage, and deploy
weapons, equipment, and personnel especially for
war purposes. They agreed that the Philippines would merely facilitate the needs and demands of the US and was practically selling its soul for free as well as making itself a target of attack by the latter´s enemies. They advocated a review and abrogation of the EDCA as they remarked that Filipinos, like the Japanese and Koreans, were against the establishment of US bases in their respective countries. They affirmed that the country could not rely on the US to defend it
against China with whom it had enormous trade relations. Rep. Dela Cruz thereafter discussed with Rep. Colmenares the role of EDCA in securing the country´s international navigational highway and in correcting all the mistakes of the VFA. Given Rep. Colmenares´
explanations, he opined that the agreement is treasonous and that both the Philippines and US
governments could be held liable to the Filipino people under the Constitution and laws of the land.(SOURCE: House Journal No.57,p.16,28 & 29)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-07
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Seneres and Dela Cruz. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: D032;
rows.title_full: JUSTICE FOR THE MURDER VICTIMS OF GATA, CAMARINES SUR
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Felix William B. Fuentebella from the Fourth... sought the intervention of the House through its oversight function regarding the cold-blooded murder of four residents of
Barangay Gata, Caramoan, Camarines Sur allegedly
committed by members of the Sagip Kalikasan Task
Force (SKTF) of Camarines Sur. He said that the
Camarines Sur provincial governor created the task force to apprehend operators of illegal mining activities therein but reportedly, the unit has been engaged in several nefarious activities. Rep. Fuentebella inquired why government agencies and the provincial government of Camarines Sur had done nothing to stop the creation of the SKTF and allowed it to engage in illegal mining activities considering the pertinent Supreme Court rulings regarding the issuances of small-scale mining permits and the fact that the SKTF is not vested with
lawful governmental authority and power. He then requested the appropriate agencies of the government such as the National Bureau of Investigation, the Philippine National Police, the Department of Justice, and the Commission on Human Rights to investigate the massacre and effect the immediate disbandment of the task force. He also proposed for a swift conviction of the perpetrators of the crime and sought the support and sympathy of the Members of the House to address the deaths of the four residents from Barangay Gata. (SOURCE: House Journal No.57,pp.26-27)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2014-06-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules.
